candidateQuestions.promptZh: 雖然這項新投資受到極大關注，但 Mei 拒絕只因為其他人都在參與便加入。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Although the investment was receiving enormous attention, Mei refused to jump on the bandwagon.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 雖然這項投資受到極大關注，但 Mei 拒絕盲目跟風加入。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The bank launched a reward programme almost identical to those of its successful competitors.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 這間銀行推出了一項獎賞計劃，內容與成功競爭對手的計劃幾乎完全相同。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: By launching a reward programme almost identical to those of its successful competitors, the bank appears to have jumped on the bandwagon.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 這間銀行推出了與成功競爭對手幾乎完全相同的獎賞計劃，看來只是跟風。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The publisher expects more writers to follow the trend now that these books are selling well.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 既然這類書籍銷情良好，出版社預期更多作家會跟隨這股潮流。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The publisher expects more writers to jump on the bandwagon now that these books are selling well.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 既然這類書籍銷情良好，出版社預期更多作家會跟隨這股潮流。

dossiers.meaningEn: Born into a royal family or a family of extremely high social rank.
dossiers.meaningZh: 出生於皇室，或出生於社會地位極高的顯赫家族。
dossiers.registerContextEn: historical writing; biographies; novels; documentaries; discussions of royalty; descriptions of fictional royal families; formal or humorous comparisons involving inherited privilege.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 在一般日常對話中，這個表達並不常用； 除非說話者刻意採用歷史、文學或幽默語氣。
dossiers.memoryEn: Purple represented imperial rank; a child born into that rank was born to the purple.
dossiers.memoryZh: 紫色象徵帝王地位；一出生便擁有這種地位的人，就是 born to the purple。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use “Born”, Not “Borne”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則二：使用 Born，不使用 Borne
semanticRules.en: Borne normally appears in other meanings of bear, such as carrying or enduring something.
semanticRules.zh: 用於出生； borne 通常用於承受、攜帶或忍受等其他意思。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Translate the Colour Literally
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四：不要按顏色逐字翻譯
semanticRules.en: Natural meaning-based translations: The answer translation must communicate social rank, not colour.
semanticRules.zh: 出生於皇室； 出身皇族； 生於帝王之家； 出身極其顯赫答案的中文翻譯必須表達社會身份，而不是顏色。

semanticRules.titleEn: Wealth Alone Is Not Enough
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：單純富有並不足夠
semanticRules.en: This shows wealth, but not royal or exceptionally high birth.
semanticRules.zh: 這句只顯示家庭富裕，並沒有顯示皇室或極高階層出身。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse Birth with Marriage
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：不要把出生與婚姻混為一談
semanticRules.en: Unless she already came from a royal family, marriage does not mean that she was born to the purple.
semanticRules.zh: 除非她本身已經出身皇室，否則透過婚姻成為公主並不代表她是 born to the purple。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse Birth with Later Success
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：不要把出身與後來成就混為一談
semanticRules.en: A soldier who becomes king through military success was not necessarily born to the purple. A businessperson who becomes extremely rich was not necessarily born to the purple.
semanticRules.zh: 一名士兵透過軍事成就成為國王，並不代表他出生於皇室。 一名商人後來變得十分富有，也不代表他出身皇室或最高貴族階層。

semanticRules.titleEn: Royal Birth Does Not Guarantee Rule
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：皇室出身不代表必然統治
semanticRules.en: be prevented by law; choose another life; lack public or political support.
semanticRules.zh: 並非每一位出生於皇室的人都會成為統治者。 某人即使出生於皇室，仍可能：

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Princess Elara entered life as a member of the ruling royal family.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 埃拉拉公主出生時已經是統治皇室的一員。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Princess Elara was born to the purple.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 埃拉拉公主出生於皇室。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The story asks whether people should receive special privilege simply because they were born into royalty.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 故事探討人們是否應僅僅因為出生於皇室而享有特殊待遇。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The story asks whether people should receive special privilege simply for being born to the purple.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 故事探討人們是否應僅僅因為出生於皇室而享有特殊待遇。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: All three sisters were princesses from birth.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 三姊妹自出生起便是公主。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: All three sisters were born to the purple.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 三姊妹全都出生於皇室。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The final scene contrasts a prince who possessed royal rank from birth with a leader who earned the people’s trust through years of service.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 最後一幕把一位出身皇室的王子，與一位透過多年服務贏得人民信任的領袖作對比。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The final scene contrasts a prince born to the purple with a leader who earned the people’s trust through years of service.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 最後一幕把一位出身皇室的王子，與一位透過多年服務贏得人民信任的領袖作對比。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Lord Adrian entered one of the country’s oldest and highest-ranking noble families at birth.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 阿德里安勳爵出生於全國其中一個最古老、地位最高的貴族家族。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Lord Adrian was born to the purple.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 阿德里安勳爵出身極其顯赫的貴族家族。

dossiers.sourcePdf: Idiom 76 - 「pigs might fly _ pigs can fly」.pdf
dossiers.meaningEn: a humorous, often sarcastic way to say that something is extremely unlikely to happen
dossiers.meaningZh: 用幽默、通常帶諷刺的語氣，表示某件事幾乎不可能發生。
dossiers.registerContextEn: conversations between friends; family conversations; light workplace conversations; fictional dialogue; humorous comments; informal messages.
dossiers.registerContextZh: pigs might fly 屬英式、非正式和幽默的表達。
dossiers.memoryEn: If the promise is as believable as a pig flying through the sky, the speaker does not believe it at all.
dossiers.memoryZh: 如果某項承諾的可信程度與豬在天空飛行一樣，便表示說話者完全不相信。

semanticRules.titleEn: The source must contain a claim, promise or prediction
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：語境必須包含說法、承諾或預測
semanticRules.en: The expression normally responds to something that another person has said or suggested.
semanticRules.zh: 這個表達通常用來回應另一個人提出的說法、承諾或預測。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do not use it to encourage somebody
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：不要用它鼓勵別人
semanticRules.en: This response would sound cruel and discouraging.
semanticRules.zh: 不適合的回應：

semanticRules.titleEn: Do not confuse it with a literal statement
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：不要與字面意思混淆
semanticRules.en: The exercise teaches only the figurative response.
semanticRules.zh: 這些豬被空運，因此牠們可以乘飛機飛行。 他說五分鐘內會完成工作——才怪呢。 本練習只教授比喻式回應。

semanticRules.titleEn: “When pigs fly” is related but not the target
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：when pigs fly 意思相關，但不是本課目標
semanticRules.en: When pigs fly has a different grammatical frame. Do not use it in the answers.
semanticRules.zh: 使用不同的句法框架，因此不可在本練習的答案中使用。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Do you think your brother might apologise? B: He has never admitted that he was wrong.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：你認為你的哥哥可能會道歉嗎？ 乙：他從未承認自己有錯。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: He might apologise, and pigs might fly.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 他可能會道歉——才怪呢。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A student who has not begun his group project says he will complete the whole thing alone before lunch.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 一名尚未開始小組項目的學生說，他會在午飯前獨自完成整個項目。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: He might finish it before lunch, and pigs might fly.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 他可能會在午飯前完成——才怪呢。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The printer breaks down every week. The manager now claims that it will work for ever without being repaired.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 打印機每星期都會故障。經理現在卻聲稱，即使不維修，它也會永遠正常運作。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The printer might work for ever without repair, and pigs might fly.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 打印機可能不用維修也能永遠運作——才怪呢。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Jade says she will wake up at five o’clock every morning, although she normally sleeps through three alarms.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 潔德說，她每天早上五時都會起床，儘管她通常連三個鬧鐘也聽不到。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Jade might wake up at five every day, and pigs might fly.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 潔德可能真的每天五時起床——才怪呢。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: After refusing to cook for twenty years, Uncle Henry promises to prepare the whole Christmas dinner. The family exchange doubtful looks.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 亨利叔叔二十年來一直拒絕下廚，現在卻承諾準備整頓聖誕晚餐。家人互相投以懷疑的目光。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Uncle Henry might cook Christmas dinner, and pigs might fly.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 亨利叔叔可能真的會準備聖誕晚餐——才怪呢。

dossiers.sourcePdf: Idiom 77 - Target Expression_ Shoulder to Shoulder.pdf
dossiers.meaningEn: People work closely together, support one another or remain united.
dossiers.meaningZh: 人們緊密合作、互相支持或團結一致。
dossiers.registerEn: Neutral to supportive; figurative or literal
dossiers.registerZh: 中性至支持；可作比喻或字面理解
dossiers.registerContextEn: People can stand physically side by side, or work and support one another in a shared effort.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 可指人們實際並肩站立，也可比喻彼此合作、互相支持。
dossiers.memoryEn: People whose shoulders form one line appear ready to face the same problem together.
dossiers.memoryZh: 當人們肩並肩排成一線時，便像是準備共同面對同一個問題。

semanticRules.en: “With + Person” Is Optional
semanticRules.zh: with + 人物是可選部分

semanticRules.titleEn: Avoid Redundant “Together”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：避免重複使用 together
semanticRules.en: Avoid Redundant “Together”
semanticRules.zh: 避免重複使用 together

semanticRules.titleEn: The Source Must Show Real Unity or
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：原句必須真正表達團結或合作
semanticRules.en: Cooperation
semanticRules.zh: 原句必須真正表達團結或合作 Suitable:

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Every Shared Activity
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：並非所有共同活動都適用
semanticRules.en: Do Not Use It for Every Shared Activity
semanticRules.zh: 並非所有共同活動都適用

semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十三：不要重複慣用語已表達的意思
semanticRules.en: Do Not Repeat the Idiom’s Meaning
semanticRules.zh: 不要重複慣用語已表達的意思

semanticRules.titleEn: Translate by Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十五：按意思翻譯
semanticRules.en: Choose the translation that matches the context.
semanticRules.zh: 肩膀對肩膀 into every answer.

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Ava and Ben worked closely together on the class poster.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 艾娃和本緊密合作，製作班級海報。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Ava and Ben worked shoulder to shoulder on the class poster.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 艾娃和本並肩合作，製作班級海報。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: To help the families, the two groups chose to work as one.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 為了幫助這些家庭，兩個小組選擇團結合作。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: To help the families, the two groups chose to work shoulder to shoulder.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 為了幫助這些家庭，兩個小組選擇並肩合作。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The two friends continued to give one another full support through every problem.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 兩位朋友在面對每個問題時都繼續全力支持對方。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Through every problem, the two friends continued to stand shoulder to shoulder.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 兩位朋友在面對每個問題時都繼續互相支持。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The parents fully supported the teachers while they planned the school trip.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 家長在老師計劃學校旅行時全力支持他們。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Shoulder to shoulder with the teachers, the parents planned the school trip.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 家長與老師並肩合作，計劃學校旅行。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Because the town faced a serious flood, people stayed united to protect their homes.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 因為小鎮面對嚴重水災，居民團結一致，保護家園。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Because the town faced a serious flood, people stood shoulder to shoulder to protect their homes.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 因為小鎮面對嚴重水災，居民團結一致，保護家園。

dossiers.editorialCaution: “Shoulder to shoulder” can be physical or figurative; these lessons target united effort. Literal proximity alone is not the same decision.

dossiers.meaningEn: A person who is willing to listen to your problems and give you sympathy, comfort, emotional support and encouragement.
dossiers.meaningZh: 一個願意聆聽你的困難，並給予同情、安慰、情緒支援及鼓勵的人。
dossiers.registerContextEn: The expression is neutral to informal and is especially natural in personal conversations, supportive messages, interviews, advice writing and discussions about relationships or emotional well-being. Dictionaries show it naturally after verbs such as need, offer and be, as well as in patterns such as see someone as or look for a shoulder to cry on.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達屬於中性至較口語的用語，尤其適合私人對話、安慰訊息、訪問、勸告文章，以及有關人際關係或情緒健康的討論。
dossiers.memoryEn: A physical shoulder supports the head; a figurative shoulder supports the person emotionally.
dossiers.memoryZh: 真正的肩膀承托頭部；比喻中的「肩膀」則承托一個人的情緒。

semanticRules.titleEn: The “Shoulder” Refers to a Person or Their Support
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：shoulder 代表一個人或其支援
semanticRules.en: The “Shoulder” Refers to a Person or Their Support
semanticRules.zh: shoulder 代表一個人或其支援

semanticRules.titleEn: Actual Tears Are Not Required
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：不一定真的流淚
semanticRules.en: He may have been disappointed without literally crying.
semanticRules.zh: 即使他沒有真的流淚，只要他需要情緒上的安慰，這個表達仍然適用。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Supporter Does Not Need to Solve the Problem
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：提供支援的人不一定要解決問題
semanticRules.en: The Supporter Does Not Need to Solve the Problem
semanticRules.zh: 提供支援的人不一定要解決問題

semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：for + 人物只是可選資料
semanticRules.en: “For + Person” Is Optional
semanticRules.zh: for + 人物只是可選資料

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Unrelated Practical Help
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：不要用來描述無關的實際協助
semanticRules.en: Do Not Use It for Unrelated Practical Help
semanticRules.zh: 不要用來描述無關的實際協助

semanticRules.titleEn: Avoid Making the Support Sound Unwelcome
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：不要把安慰寫成對方不願接受的行為
semanticRules.en: Avoid Making the Support Sound Unwelcome
semanticRules.zh: 不要把安慰寫成對方不願接受的行為

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Sophie failed her driving test. She wanted someone who would listen kindly and comfort her.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 蘇菲考車失敗了。她希望有人願意親切地聆聽和安慰她。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Sophie needed a shoulder to cry on after failing her driving test.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 蘇菲考車失敗後，需要一個可以傾訴和尋求安慰的人。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Whenever Ethan was disappointed, his grandfather listened patiently and comforted him.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 每當伊森感到失望時，祖父都會耐心聆聽和安慰他。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: For Ethan, his grandfather was a shoulder to cry on after every disappointment.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 對伊森而言，每當他感到失望時，祖父都是他可以傾訴和尋求安慰的人。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The teacher believed that worried pupils could speak openly to the school adviser and receive emotional support.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 老師相信，感到擔心的學生可以坦誠地向校內輔導員傾訴，並得到情緒支援。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The teacher saw the school adviser as a shoulder to cry on for worried pupils.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 老師把校內輔導員視為擔心的學生可以傾訴和尋求安慰的人。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: During a difficult week, the neighbour unexpectedly turned out to be a kind and supportive listener.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 在艱難的一星期裏，那名鄰居出乎意料地成為一個親切而願意支持別人的聆聽者。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Her neighbour proved to be a shoulder to cry on during the difficult week.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 在艱難的一星期裏，她的鄰居原來是一個願意聆聽和安慰她的人。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Sometimes an upset person benefits more from sympathy and quiet listening than from a long list of solutions.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 有時候，對一個難過的人而言，同情和安靜聆聽比一長串解決方法更有幫助。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: A shoulder to cry on can sometimes help more than a list of solutions.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 有時候，一個願意聆聽和安慰自己的人，比一連串解決方法更有幫助。

dossiers.meaningEn: You have heard or learned some information from another person, but you do not want to reveal who gave you the information.
dossiers.meaningZh: 你從某人那裡得知了一些消息，但你不想透露究竟是誰告訴你的。
dossiers.registerContextEn: playful; teasing; friendly; slightly mysterious; deliberately vague.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達主要用於非正式對話，常帶有：
dossiers.memoryEn: Imagine a tiny bird quietly bringing you a secret. You know the information, but the real source remains hidden.
dossiers.memoryZh: 想像一隻小鳥悄悄把秘密帶給你：你知道消息，但真正的消息來源仍然保密。

semanticRules.zh: 不要過度使用

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Someone told me privately that your birthday is tomorrow, but I am not going to say who.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 有人私下告訴我你的生日是明天，但我不會說是誰。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: A little bird told me that your birthday is tomorrow.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 有人告訴我你的生日是明天，不過我不會透露是誰。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: When the children asked their father how he knew exactly which toy they wanted, he gave them a playful answer instead of naming their mother.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 孩子問爸爸怎麼會知道他們究竟想要哪件玩具時，他沒有說是媽媽告訴他的，只是開玩笑地回答。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Their father smiled and said, “A little bird told me.”
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 爸爸笑著說：「有人告訴我的，不過我不說是誰。」

candidateQuestions.promptEn: You want to know where I heard about the new timetable. I am keeping that information private.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 你想知道我是從哪裡聽說新時間表的，但我不打算透露消息來源。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: As for how I know about the new timetable, a little bird told me.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 至於我是怎樣知道新時間表的，有人告訴我的，不過消息來源無可奉告。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: I had already bought a card before Ben announced his engagement because somebody had privately given me the news.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: Ben 公布訂婚消息前，我已經買好了賀卡，因為有人私下告訴我。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I had already bought a card because a little bird told me about Ben’s engagement.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我早已買好了賀卡，因為有人私下告訴我 Ben 訂婚的消息。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: How could you possibly know that I had chosen the red one? B: I have my sources, and I am not giving you any names.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：你怎麼可能知道我選了紅色那件？ 乙：我有自己的消息來源，而且我不會告訴你任何名字。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Let’s just say a little bird told me which one you had chosen.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 就當作是有人偷偷告訴我你選了哪一件吧。

dossiers.meaningEn: to be brave enough to undertake a dangerous or difficult action that is necessary or beneficial to a group, especially when everyone supports the idea but nobody wants to accept the risk
dossiers.meaningZh: 勇敢承擔一項危險或困難、但對整個群體有需要或有好處的行動；尤其指眾人都贊成某個做法， 卻沒有人願意承擔實行時的風險
dossiers.registerContextEn: Register: neutral, figurative and somewhat traditional
dossiers.registerContextZh: 語域：中性、比喻性，並帶有較傳統的色彩
dossiers.memoryEn: Everyone wants the warning bell, but somebody must risk approaching the cat.
dossiers.memoryZh: 所有人都想要警報鈴，但必須有人冒險走近貓隻。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Action Must Involve Genuine Risk
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則三：行動必須涉及真正風險
semanticRules.en: A worker reports a dangerous machine even though the manager may punish her. A student volunteers to clean the board.
semanticRules.zh: 一名工人舉報危險機器，即使經理可能懲罰她。 一名學生自願清潔白板。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Action Should Benefit a Group or Shared Cause
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四：行動應對群體或共同目標有益
semanticRules.en: One nurse reports the wrong medicine labels to protect the patients.
semanticRules.zh: 一名護士舉報錯誤的藥物標籤，以保障病人。 他為自己購買新電話。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Start the Ball Rolling”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五
semanticRules.en: start the ball rolling bell the cat
semanticRules.zh: 不要與 start the ball rolling 混淆採取令一個過程開始的第一步承擔其他人不願面對的危險或風險

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Take One for the Team”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六
semanticRules.en: take one for the team bell the cat
semanticRules.zh: 不要與 take one for the team 混淆為團隊承受損失或作出犧牲採取處理問題所需的危險行動

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Idiom’s Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：不要重複解釋慣用語
semanticRules.en: Do Not Repeat the Idiom’s Meaning
semanticRules.zh: 不要重複解釋慣用語

semanticRules.titleEn: Keep Important Context
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：保留重要情境
semanticRules.en: Keep Important Context
semanticRules.zh: 保留重要情境

candidateQuestions.promptEn: All the workers knew that the old lift was unsafe, but none of them was brave enough to tell the owner.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 所有工人都知道舊升降機並不安全，但沒有人有勇氣告訴店主。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: None of the workers was brave enough to bell the cat and tell the owner that the old lift was unsafe.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 沒有一名工人敢挺身承擔風險，告訴店主舊升降機並不安全。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The players expected their captain to risk speaking to the referee about the unfair decision for the whole team.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 球員期望隊長承擔風險，代表整個團隊向裁判反映不公平的判決。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The players expected their captain to bell the cat and speak to the referee about the unfair decision.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 球員期望隊長承擔風險，向裁判反映不公平的判決。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: One resident agreed to be the first person to sign the letter so that the dangerous road could finally be reported.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 一名居民同意率先簽署信件，讓危險道路的問題終於可以得到舉報。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: To bell the cat, one resident agreed to be the first to sign the letter about the dangerous road.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 為了挺身承擔風險，一名居民同意率先簽署有關危險道路的信件。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The medicine labels are wrong, and one nurse must report the problem before someone is harmed.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 藥物標籤出錯，必須有一名護士在有人受傷前舉報問題。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: One nurse must bell the cat and report the wrong medicine labels before someone is harmed.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 必須有一名護士挺身承擔風險，在有人受傷前舉報錯誤的藥物標籤。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Although every shop owner supported reporting the threats, nobody volunteered to make the call.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 雖然每名店主都支持舉報威脅行為，但沒有人自願致電舉報。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Although every shop owner supported the idea, nobody volunteered to bell the cat and report the threats.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 雖然每名店主都支持這個做法，但沒有人自願承擔風險舉報威脅行為。

dossiers.meaningEn: A person, belief, custom, rule, system, organisation or institution that people treat as too important to question, criticise or change, often without a good reason.
dossiers.meaningZh: 某個人物、信念、習俗、規則、制度、組織或機構受到過分保護，以致人們不敢質疑、批評或改變它，而且這種特殊待遇往往缺乏合理理由。
dossiers.registerContextEn: workplace discussions; public speeches; opinion writing; political and social commentary; discussions about schools, companies and organisations.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達屬於較口語至中性的用語，而且明顯帶有批評意味。
dossiers.memoryEn: A literally protected cow becomes the image of an idea or institution that people are afraid to touch, question or criticise.
dossiers.memoryZh: 一隻受到特殊保護的牛，成為一個比喻畫面，用來代表人們不敢觸碰、質疑或批評的觀念或機構。

semanticRules.titleEn: Respect Is Not Enough
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：受到尊重並不足夠
semanticRules.en: Everyone respects the teacher because she works hard. Nothing suggests that people are afraid to question or criticise her. Everyone is afraid to criticise the teacher, even when she makes a mistake.
semanticRules.zh: 大家都尊重那名老師，因為她工作努力。 句子並沒有表示人們不敢質疑或批評她。 即使那名老師犯錯，所有人仍不敢批評她。 那名老師被視為不可批評的人物。

semanticRules.titleEn: Being Old Is Not Enough
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：歷史悠久並不足夠
semanticRules.en: The festival is one hundred years old. The festival is one hundred years old, and nobody is willing to discuss changing it.
semanticRules.zh: 這個節慶活動已有一百年歷史。 這個節慶活動已有一百年歷史，而且沒有人願意討論作出改動。 這個節慶活動已成為不容改動的傳統。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Meaning Unnecessarily
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：不要不必要地重複意思
semanticRules.en: The final clause simply explains the idiom again. The idiom itself carries the protected-from-criticism meaning.
semanticRules.zh: 句末部分只是再次解釋慣用語的意思。 這項規則是學校不容質疑的制度。 慣用語本身已經包含「不容批評或質疑」的意思。

semanticRules.titleEn: Avoid Literal Chinese Translation
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：避免逐字翻譯
semanticRules.en: Do not translate the idiom as: In figurative contexts, translate the intended meaning:
semanticRules.zh: 一隻神聖的牛不容質疑的制度； 不可批評的人物； 不容改動的傳統； 受到過分保護的觀念

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Holy Cow”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十三：不要與 holy cow 混淆
semanticRules.en: A person, belief or institution protected from criticism. An expression of surprise. They are not interchangeable.
semanticRules.zh: 不容批評的人物、信念或機構。 表達驚訝的感嘆語。 兩者不能互換。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: No one at the school is willing to question the old uniform rule.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 學校裏沒有人願意質疑舊有的校服規定。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The old uniform rule is a sacred cow at the school.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 學校把舊有的校服規定視為不可質疑的制度。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The programme has operated for many years. Some writers say that it receives too much respect and is never properly examined.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 這個計劃已推行多年。有些作者認為，它受到過分尊重，而且從未得到適當檢討。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Some writers have called the long-running programme a sacred cow.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 有些作者把這個長期推行的計劃稱為不容質疑的制度。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Must our family dinner always follow exactly the same plan? B: No. We are allowed to change a tradition.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：我們的家庭晚餐一定要永遠遵照完全相同的安排嗎？ 乙：不用。我們可以改變傳統。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Sunday dinner does not have to be a sacred cow in our family.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 星期日晚餐不必成為我們家中不可改動的傳統。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The founder created the company slogan, so workers are afraid to suggest changing it.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 公司標語由創辦人創作，因此員工不敢建議作出改動。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Because the founder created it, the company slogan is treated as a sacred cow.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 由於公司標語由創辦人創作，它被視為不可改動的事物。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The senior worker is protected from all criticism, and this is unfair to the rest of the team.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 那名資深員工不受任何批評，這對其他隊員並不公平。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Treating the senior worker as a sacred cow is unfair to the rest of the team.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 把那名資深員工視為不可批評的人物，對其他隊員並不公平。

dossiers.lemma: Walk on Eggs / Walk on Eggshells
dossiers.sourcePdf: Idiom 82 - 「Walk on Eggs _ Walk on Eggshells」.pdf
dossiers.meaningEn: to speak or act with great care because you fear upsetting someone or making a tense situation worse
dossiers.meaningZh: 因害怕觸怒他人或令緊張情況惡化，說話做事時步步為營。
dossiers.registerZh: 適合談話；須留意關係語境
dossiers.registerContextEn: news reports; writing about relationships or group atmosphere.
dossiers.registerContextZh: walk on eggshells 屬於非正式至中性的表達，常見於日常對話、個人敘述、工作討論、訪問、新聞報道，以及描述關係或團隊氣氛的文章。
dossiers.fixed: Walk on Eggs / Walk on Eggshells
dossiers.memoryEn: One careless step could break an egg; one careless word could upset the person.
dossiers.memoryZh: 一步不小心便可能踩破雞蛋；一句說話不小心便可能觸怒對方。

semanticRules.titleEn: It Usually Concerns a Person’s Reaction
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四：通常涉及某人的反應
semanticRules.en: The person may be stated directly or understood from the context.
semanticRules.zh: 我們在他身邊說話處處小心，因為他很容易發怒。 引起這種小心反應的人可以直接說明，也可以從語境得知。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Ordinary Physical Care
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：不要用於一般身體上的小心
semanticRules.en: The sentence concerns literal physical care, not fear of upsetting someone. I carried the glass very carefully.
semanticRules.zh: 這句話只是表示拿着玻璃杯時小心，並不涉及害怕令某人不高興。 我非常小心地拿着玻璃杯。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Every Polite Conversation
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：不要用於每場有禮貌的對話
semanticRules.en: Ordinary politeness does not necessarily mean somebody is walking on eggshells. The expression requires stronger tension, nervousness or fear.
semanticRules.zh: 一般的禮貌並不代表某人在戰戰兢兢地說話。 這個表達需要較強的緊張、不安或害怕情緒。

semanticRules.titleEn: “Around + Person” Is Optional
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：around + person 是可選部分
semanticRules.en: Both are grammatically complete.
semanticRules.zh: 我們當時說話處處小心。 我們當時在經理面前說話處處小心。 兩句在文法上都完整。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Walk on Thin Ice”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：不要與 walk on thin ice 混淆
semanticRules.en: Walk on eggshells usually focuses on being careful not to upset somebody. Walk on thin ice usually means being in a risky position where one may soon face trouble. The expressions can overlap, but they are not freely interchangeable.
semanticRules.zh: walk on eggshells 通常強調小心避免令某人不高興。 walk on thin ice 通常表示某人正處於危險處境，可能很快便會遇上麻煩。 兩個表達可能有部分重疊，但不能在所有情況下自由互換。

semanticRules.titleEn: A Healthy Situation Should Not Require Constant Fear
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：健康環境不應令人長期害怕
semanticRules.en: It should not be taught as though fear-based communication were normal or desirable.
semanticRules.zh: 僱員不應該只為了提出合理問題而戰戰兢兢。 教學時不應把這種由害怕造成的溝通方式說成正常或理想。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Everyone speaks very carefully around Owen because he becomes upset over small comments.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 大家在歐文身邊說話都非常小心，因為一些小評論也會令他不高興。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Everyone walks on eggshells around Owen because he becomes upset over small comments.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 大家在歐文身邊說話都處處小心，因為一些小評論也會令他不高興。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: I want meetings where people can disagree openly and do not need to fear upsetting the manager.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 我希望會議容許大家公開提出不同意見，而不需要害怕令經理不高興。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I want meetings where people can disagree openly without having to walk on eggshells around the manager.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我希望會議容許大家公開提出不同意見，而不需要在經理面前戰戰兢兢。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: I am tired of watching every word because you become angry so easily.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：我厭倦了每句說話都要小心，因為你實在太容易發怒。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I’m tired of walking on eggshells around you because you become angry so easily.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我厭倦了在你面前每句說話都要小心，因為你實在太容易發怒。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Being extremely careful may prevent one argument tonight, but it cannot solve the real communication problem.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 極度小心可能可以避免今晚的一場爭執，但不能解決真正的溝通問題。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Walking on eggshells may prevent one argument tonight, but it cannot solve the real communication problem.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 步步為營可能可以避免今晚的一場爭執，但不能解決真正的溝通問題。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The group no longer wanted to speak with extreme care, so they asked the leader to set clear rules.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 小組不想再說話時處處小心，因此要求領袖制定清楚規則。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Not wanting to walk on eggshells any longer, the group asked the leader to set clear rules.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 小組不想再說話時處處小心，因此要求領袖制定清楚規則。

dossiers.editorialCaution: Preferred classroom form is “walk on eggshells”; source explicitly accepts “walk on eggs” as a valid alternative. Neither may be a false wrong option.

dossiers.meaningEn: To be at an important and uncertain stage when a person, group, organisation or situation must choose which direction to take.
dossiers.meaningZh: 處於重要而未明朗的關頭，需要決定下一步應走哪個方向。
dossiers.registerContextEn: everyday conversation; workplace discussions; presentations; interviews; news and commentary; general formal writing; personal reflection.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 固定部分 at the crossroads
dossiers.memoryEn: Different roads lead to different destinations; different decisions lead to different futures.
dossiers.memoryZh: 不同道路通往不同目的地；不同決定帶來不同未來。

semanticRules.titleEn: It Must Be an Important Decision
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則一：必須涉及重要決定
semanticRules.en: Choosing a drink is usually too minor to justify the idiom. A humorous speaker might deliberately exaggerate, but humorous exaggeration is not taught in this exercise.
semanticRules.zh: 正面臨到外國工作還是留在家人身邊的重要抉擇。 正面臨點茶還是咖啡的抉擇。 選擇飲品通常太微不足道，不足以使用這個慣用語。 說話者有時可能故意誇張以製造幽默效果，但本練習不教授這種用法。

semanticRules.titleEn: More Than One Future Direction Must Be Possible
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則二：未來必須有多於一個可能方向
semanticRules.en: More Than One Future Direction Must Be Possible
semanticRules.zh: 學校必須決定維修舊校舍還是搬往其他地方，正面臨重要抉擇。 學校已作出選擇，因此已不再處於抉擇關頭。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It Merely for a Difficult Situation
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則三：不要只因情況困難便使用
semanticRules.en: The shop is losing money and must choose between closing and changing its business. The shop was very busy today. The second sentence contains no important choice about the future.
semanticRules.zh: 店舖正在虧蝕，必須在結業和改變經營方式之間作出選擇。 店舖今天十分繁忙。 第二句並沒有涉及對未來的重要選擇。

semanticRules.titleEn: “Reach a Crossroads” Is Related but Not the
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六
semanticRules.en: Target She has reached a crossroads in her career.
semanticRules.zh: reach a crossroads 意思相關但不是指定答案規則六：reach a crossroads 意思相關但不是指定答案 Natural English: 她的事業已來到重要關頭。 她的事業正處於重要關頭。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with the Meeting of Two Fields
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：不要與兩個領域的交匯混淆
semanticRules.en: being at a point where an important direction must be chosen It does not teach the separate use in which crossroads simply describes where subjects, cultures or fields meet.
semanticRules.zh: 本練習教授： 本練習不教授 crossroads 純粹表示學科、文化或領域交匯點的另一種用法。

semanticRules.titleEn: Avoid Accidental Literal Meanings
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：避免意外產生字面意思
semanticRules.en: In this exercise, every answer must use the figurative decision-point meaning.
semanticRules.zh: 我們在十字路口停下來查看地圖。 我們正處於關鍵時刻，必須決定項目的未來。 在本練習中，所有答案都必須使用「面臨重要抉擇」的比喻意思。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: I have to choose between becoming a teacher and working as a designer. This choice could shape my whole career.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 我必須在成為老師和從事設計工作之間作出選擇。這項選擇可能會影響我的整個事業。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I am at the crossroads in my career and must choose between teaching and design.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我的事業正處於重要關頭，必須在教學和設計工作之間作出選擇。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Why has the charity not made its plans for next year? B: It is waiting to learn whether its main supporter will continue giving money.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：慈善機構為甚麼仍未制訂明年的計劃？ 乙：它正在等待主要支持者會否繼續捐款。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The charity remains at the crossroads while it waits to learn whether its main supporter will continue giving money.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 慈善機構在等待主要支持者會否繼續捐款期間，仍處於重要抉擇的關頭。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Town leaders say the bus service has reached a stage where they must either improve it or end it.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 鎮上主管表示，巴士服務已來到必須改善或結束的階段。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The town leaders believe the bus service is at the crossroads: they must either improve it or end it.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 鎮上主管認為巴士服務正處於重要關頭：他們必須選擇改善還是結束服務。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Have you decided whether to take the office job or work from home? B: Not yet. Both choices could completely change my daily life.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：你決定接受辦公室工作還是在家工作了嗎？ 乙：還未。兩個選擇都可能完全改變我的日常生活。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Not yet. I am at the crossroads between taking the office job and working from home.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 還未決定。我正面臨接受辦公室工作還是在家工作的重要抉擇。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Why do you think we have reached such an important decision point? B: The old plan has failed, but a better opportunity may also have appeared.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：你為甚麼認為我們已來到如此重要的抉擇關頭？ 乙：舊計劃已失敗，但也可能出現了一個更好的機會。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Are we at the crossroads because the old plan has failed, or because a better opportunity has appeared?
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我們正處於重要抉擇的關頭，是因為舊計劃失敗，還是因為出現了更好的機會？

dossiers.meaningEn: To be very brave, confident or willing to do something difficult, frightening, uncomfortable or socially risky.
dossiers.meaningZh: 很有勇氣或膽量，願意做一件困難、令人害怕、令人不安或需要勇氣面對他人的事情。
dossiers.registerContextEn: usually approving; natural in conversation, interviews, sports discussion and informal messages; less suitable for formal reports, academic essays or official letters.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 雖然這個表達通常帶有稱讚語氣，但實際意思仍取決於語調及語境。 在某些帶有衝突的情境中， 類似說法可能帶有諷刺意味，或暗示某人過分大膽。 本練習只教授表示真正勇氣的正面意思。
dossiers.memoryEn: Do not picture many physical bottles. Picture somebody with enough courage to act when others hesitate.
dossiers.memoryZh: 不要想像很多實體瓶子。應想像一個人在其他人猶豫時，仍有足夠勇氣採取行動。

semanticRules.titleEn: Courage Is Not Recklessness
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：勇氣並不等於魯莽
semanticRules.en: Dangerous or careless behaviour should not automatically be praised as courage.
semanticRules.zh: 她冷靜報告危險故障時十分有勇氣。 他遠超速駕駛，所以很有膽量。 危險或不顧後果的行為，不應自動被稱讚為有勇氣。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Same Meaning Mechanically
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：不要機械式重複同一意思
semanticRules.en: The second half simply defines the idiom again. The action provides evidence rather than repeating the definition.
semanticRules.zh: 後半部分只是再次解釋慣用語的意思。 嘉賓變得憤怒後，她仍繼續訪問，十分有膽量。 這項行動提供了勇氣的證據，而不是再次重複定義。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Bottle Up”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：不要與 bottle up 混淆
semanticRules.en: = possess considerable courage = bottle up one’s feelings These expressions have different meanings and grammar.
semanticRules.zh: 很有膽量 = prevent oneself from expressing feelings = 把感受抑壓在心裏這兩個表達的意思及文法都不同。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Lena felt nervous, but she still gave a speech to the whole school.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 莉娜感到緊張，但仍在全校師生面前發表演說。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Lena has a lot of bottle; she gave the speech even though she was nervous.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 莉娜很有膽量；即使感到緊張，她仍完成了演說。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Brave people are often willing to speak when everybody else remains silent.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 勇敢的人往往願意在其他人都保持沉默時發言。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: People who have a lot of bottle are often willing to speak when others remain silent.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 很有膽量的人往往願意在其他人保持沉默時發言。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: For the final round of the debating competition, the coach wanted a player who would not be frightened by pressure.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 在辯論比賽的最後一輪，教練希望派出一名不會被壓力嚇倒的隊員。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The coach wanted a player who had a lot of bottle for the final round of the debating competition.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 教練希望在辯論比賽最後一輪派出一名很有膽量的隊員。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The youngest speaker surprised us by answering every question calmly and without fear.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 最年輕的講者毫不畏懼地冷靜回答每條問題，令我們十分驚訝。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: What impressed us was that the youngest speaker had a lot of bottle and answered every question calmly.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 最令我們佩服的是，最年輕的講者很有膽量，而且冷靜地回答每條問題。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The guest became angry, but the interviewer found the courage to continue asking questions.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 嘉賓變得憤怒，但訪問者仍鼓起勇氣繼續提問。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: She must have had a lot of bottle to continue the interview after the guest became angry.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 嘉賓變得憤怒後，她仍繼續訪問，一定很有膽量。

dossiers.meaningEn: To become or feel suddenly nervous, frightened or uncertain about something that you had planned or agreed to do, often causing you to hesitate, delay or withdraw.
dossiers.meaningZh: 對原本計劃或答應要做的事情突然感到緊張、害怕或不確定，因而猶豫、拖延或臨陣退縮。
dossiers.registerContextEn: everyday conversation; workplace discussion; interviews; news reports; general writing; discussions about decisions, performances, travel, purchases and commitments.
dossiers.registerContextZh: Cold feet 屬於非正式但十分常見的表達，可自然用於日常對話、工作討論、訪問、新聞報道及一般文章。
dossiers.memoryEn: A person with cold feet is no longer ready to step forward.
dossiers.memoryZh: 有 cold feet 的人，已經不再敢踏出下一步。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Say “Be Cold Feet”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則二：不可說 be cold feet
semanticRules.en: Do Not Say “Be Cold Feet”
semanticRules.zh: 原因是臨陣退縮，而不是時間不足。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Plan Must Already Exist
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四：必須已有原定計劃
semanticRules.en: planned to do; agreed to do; intended to do; was expected to do; had already begun arranging. The second person has not lost courage about an existing plan. He simply has no plan or desire to perform.
semanticRules.zh: 這個慣用語通常描述某人對已計劃、已答應、原本打算或預期要做的事情突然感到膽怯。 他答應表演，卻在演出前臨陣退縮。 第二個人並不是對原定計劃失去勇氣； 他根本沒有表演的計劃或意願。

semanticRules.titleEn: It Is Stronger Than Ordinary Nervousness
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：語氣比一般緊張更強
semanticRules.en: Cold feet normally suggests that the nervousness may affect whether the person continues.
semanticRules.zh: cold feet 通常表示緊張可能影響某人會否繼續原定行動。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use “Got”, Not “Gotten”, in This British English Set
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：本英式英語練習使用 got，而非 gotten
semanticRules.en: Every answer in this exercise follows British English.
semanticRules.zh: 本練習的所有答案均採用英式英語。

semanticRules.titleEn: People and Organisations Can Get Cold Feet
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：個人及機構都可以 get cold feet
semanticRules.en: People and Organisations Can Get Cold Feet
semanticRules.zh: 公司開始對這個項目感到動搖。

semanticRules.titleEn: Avoid Accidental Literal Meanings
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：避免意外產生字面意思
semanticRules.en: Her feet were cold because her shoes were wet. The surrounding context must establish nervousness, fear or uncertainty—not temperature.
semanticRules.zh: 她的鞋濕了，所以雙腳感到寒冷。 她在比賽前臨陣退縮。 周圍語境必須清楚表示緊張、恐懼或動搖，而不是身體溫度。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Ava intended to give a speech at school, but she became too nervous when her name was called and did not go on stage.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: Ava 原本打算在學校發表演講，但被叫到名字時突然過分緊張，沒有走上台。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Ava got cold feet before the school speech.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: Ava 在學校演講前臨陣退縮。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Why is Omar still working at the same company? B: He wanted to leave, but fear stopped him from accepting another job.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：Omar 為甚麼仍在同一間公司工作？ 乙：他原本想離開，但因為害怕而沒有接受另一份工作。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Omar’s cold feet about leaving a safe job kept him at the company.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: Omar 因為不敢離開穩定的工作，所以繼續留在公司。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The coach said that Sam had lost his courage immediately before the final and had asked not to play.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 教練說，Sam 在決賽前突然失去勇氣，並要求不要出場。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The coach said Sam had got cold feet before the final.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 教練說 Sam 在決賽前臨陣退縮。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Eric remained calm and signed the agreement despite pressure from several people.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 儘管受到多人的壓力，Eric 仍保持冷靜並簽署協議。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: There was no sign of cold feet as Eric signed the agreement.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: Eric 簽署協議時，完全沒有臨陣退縮的跡象。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: After seeing that the project would cost much more than expected, the investors began to hesitate and consider withdrawing.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 投資者發現項目成本遠高於預期後，開始猶豫並考慮退出。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Higher costs have given investors cold feet about the new housing project.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 成本上升令投資者開始對這個新住宅項目感到動搖。

dossiers.meaningEn: To stop using, consuming or doing something suddenly and completely, instead of reducing it gradually.
dossiers.meaningZh: 突然並完全停止使用、進食、飲用或進行某件事，而不是逐步減少。
dossiers.registerContextEn: everyday conversation; personal stories; interviews; informal articles; discussions about habits; friendly advice; light-hearted comments about technology or food.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 帶有較口語的色彩，但普遍容易理解，常見於日常對話、個人故事、訪問、非正式文章和有關習慣的討論
dossiers.memoryEn: Think of one immediate, complete break: no gradual reduction and no middle stage.
dossiers.memoryZh: 把它想像成一次即時而徹底的中斷：沒有逐步減少，也沒有中間階段。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Stop Must Be Complete
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則一：必須完全停止
semanticRules.en: Ella gradually cut down on coffee.
semanticRules.zh: 一下子完全戒掉咖啡。 每天少喝一杯咖啡。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Stop Must Be Sudden
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則二：必須突然停止
semanticRules.en: The Stop Must Be Sudden
semanticRules.zh: 他在星期一突然完全停用該應用程式。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Quit Cold Turkey”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：不要與 quit cold turkey 混合
semanticRules.en: Do Not Confuse It with “Quit Cold Turkey”
semanticRules.zh: 不要與 quit cold turkey 混合

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Add a Literal Turkey
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：不要理解成真正的火雞
semanticRules.en: Do Not Add a Literal Turkey
semanticRules.zh: 不要理解成真正的火雞

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Idiom’s Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：不要重複慣用語已表達的意思
semanticRules.en: Do Not Repeat the Idiom’s Meaning
semanticRules.zh: 一下子完全戒掉朱古力。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use It for a Meaningful Habit
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：用於有一定持續性的習慣
semanticRules.en: Use It for a Meaningful Habit
semanticRules.zh: 用於有一定持續性的習慣

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Ethan drank energy drinks every day, but he stopped completely and suddenly after his final exam.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: Ethan 每天都喝能量飲品，但他在期末考試後突然完全停止飲用。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Ethan went cold turkey on energy drinks after his final exam.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: Ethan 在期末考試後一下子戒掉了能量飲品。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Ella may stop drinking coffee all at once instead of reducing it slowly.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: Ella 可能會一下子完全停止喝咖啡，而不是逐步減少。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Ella might go cold turkey on coffee instead of reducing it slowly.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: Ella 可能會突然完全戒掉咖啡，而不是逐步減少。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The office team decided that completely stopping work messages after 8 p.m. was easier than setting many small rules.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 辦公室團隊認為，晚上八時後完全停止傳送工作訊息，比制定許多小規則容易。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The office team decided that going cold turkey on work messages after 8 p.m. was easier than setting many small rules.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 辦公室團隊認為，晚上八時後徹底停止工作訊息，比制定許多小規則容易。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Felix suggested that everyone completely stop unnecessary online shopping until they had saved enough money.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: Felix 建議大家完全停止不必要的網上購物，直至儲夠金錢。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: “Let’s go cold turkey on unnecessary online shopping until we save enough,” Felix suggested.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: Felix 建議：「讓我們徹底停止不必要的網上購物，直至儲夠金錢。」

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The class completely stopped using phones during lunch. Afterwards, the students spent more time talking.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 全班在午膳時完全停止使用手機。其後，學生花更多時間交談。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: After the class went cold turkey on phones during lunch, the students spent more time talking.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 全班在午膳時徹底停用手機後，學生花更多時間交談。

dossiers.meaningEn: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.
dossiers.meaningZh: 突然感到一陣恐懼、不安或擔心；因為一件突如其來或令人害怕的事情而感到一陣發熱發冷。
dossiers.registerContextEn: conversation; personal stories; descriptions of frightening experiences; informal writing; interviews; fiction and narrative writing.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達屬於中性至非正式用語，尤其常見於日常對話、個人經歷、故事及對恐懼反應的描述。
dossiers.memoryEn: A frightening thought makes the body seem to change from hot to cold in an instant.
dossiers.memoryZh: 一個可怕的念頭，彷彿令身體在一瞬間由熱變冷。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Blow Hot and Cold”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則三：不要與 blow hot and cold 混淆
semanticRules.en: sudden fear or worry frequently change one’s opinion or attitude The company blew hot and cold about the plan for six months.
semanticRules.zh: 突然感到恐懼或不安反覆改變意見或態度公司在六個月內對該計劃的態度反覆不定。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Trigger Must Be Frightening or Worrying
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：觸發事件必須令人害怕或擔心
semanticRules.en: a late-night phone call; a police officer saying your name; a missing child or pet; an unexpected hospital message; a strange noise; an emergency alarm; the thought that an important item is missing; suddenly realising that something has gone wrong.
semanticRules.zh: 適合的觸發情況包括深夜來電、警員叫出自己的名字、孩子或寵物失蹤、醫院突然來電、奇怪聲音、緊急警報，或突然察覺事情出錯。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Same Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：不要重複相同意思
semanticRules.en: Go hot and cold already communicates the sudden fearful reaction. The second part unnecessarily explains the idiom again.
semanticRules.zh: 已經包含突然感到恐懼的意思，不應在後面再次重複解釋。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use It Naturally, Not Everywhere
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：自然使用，不要過度使用
semanticRules.en: is tired; is slightly nervous; changes their mind; dislikes something; becomes angry.
semanticRules.zh: 只有當某人因意外、危險或令人擔心的事情而突然感到強烈恐懼或不安時，才適合使用這個表達。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: When the phone rang after midnight, I suddenly felt a strong wave of fear.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 電話在半夜後響起時，我頓時感到非常害怕。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I went hot and cold when the phone rang after midnight.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 電話在半夜後響起時，我頓時感到非常害怕。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The manager asked the new worker one quiet question. It immediately caused the worker to feel frightened.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 經理平靜地問了新員工一條問題，令他立即感到害怕。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The manager’s quiet question made the new worker go hot and cold.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 經理平靜的一條問題令新員工頓時感到害怕。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Even now, remembering how close the car came to us gives me the same sudden feeling of fear.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 即使到了現在，我想起那輛車曾經如此接近我們，仍會突然感到害怕。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I still go hot and cold when I remember how close the car came to us.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我現在每次想起那輛車曾經如此接近我們，仍會突然感到害怕。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: I heard breaking glass downstairs last night. B: Would a sound like that also make you suddenly feel afraid?
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：昨晚我聽到樓下有玻璃碎裂的聲音。 乙：那種聲音也會令你頓時感到害怕嗎？
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Could the sound of breaking glass make you go hot and cold too?
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 玻璃碎裂的聲音也會令你頓時感到害怕嗎？

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: What happened when the head teacher called you into the office? B: I suddenly became very frightened because I thought I was in serious trouble.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：校長叫你進辦公室時，發生了甚麼事？ 乙：我以為自己闖了大禍，所以頓時感到非常害怕。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I went hot and cold because I thought I was in serious trouble.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我以為自己闖了大禍，所以頓時感到非常害怕。

dossiers.editorialCaution: Check which “go hot and cold” sense the source questions actually use. Do not import a different temperature or vacillation sense by title alone.

dossiers.meaningEn: a person or thing that appears harmless or helpful but secretly aims to weaken or attack a group from within
dossiers.meaningZh: 表面無害或有用，實際卻被用來從內部欺騙、削弱或攻擊某個群體的人或事物。
dossiers.registerContextEn: Cambridge labels the expression literary, while Collins marks the figurative meaning as disapproving.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達屬中性至正式用語，有時帶有文學色彩，而且通常包含強烈的負面批評。 它常見於新聞、公共討論、工作分析和嚴肅對話。
dossiers.memoryEn: The horse looked like a gift, entered the city and released a hidden danger from within.
dossiers.memoryZh: 木馬看來是一份禮物，獲准進入城內，然後從內部釋放隱藏的危險。

semanticRules.titleEn: There Must Be a Harmless or Helpful Appearance
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則一：必須具有無害或有益的外表
semanticRules.en: There Must Be a Harmless or Helpful Appearance
semanticRules.zh: 這項提議表面慷慨，實際暗藏控制學會的目的。

semanticRules.titleEn: There Must Be a Hidden Harmful Purpose
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則二：必須具有隱藏的有害目的
semanticRules.en: A person is not a Trojan horse merely because they are new, quiet, unpopular or from another group.
semanticRules.zh: 一個人不會只是因為新加入、安靜、不受歡迎或來自另一個團體，便成為 a Trojan horse。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Expression May Describe a Person or a Thing
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四：這個表達可以形容人物或事物
semanticRules.en: The Expression May Describe a Person or a Thing
semanticRules.zh: 這個表達可以形容人物或事物

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Entire Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：不要完整重複慣用語的意思
semanticRules.en: Do Not Repeat the Entire Meaning
semanticRules.zh: 不要完整重複慣用語的意思

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with the Computing Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：不要與電腦用語混淆
semanticRules.en: Do Not Confuse It with the Computing Meaning
semanticRules.zh: 不要與電腦用語混淆

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Ava joined the drama club and acted helpful, but she secretly sent its plans to a rival school.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 艾娃加入戲劇學會後表現得十分熱心，卻暗中把學會的計劃傳給敵對學校。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Ava was a Trojan horse within the drama club, secretly sending its plans to a rival school.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 艾娃其實是敵對學校安插在戲劇學會內的棋子，暗中把學會的計劃傳出去。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The donation looked kind, but it gave the larger company enough influence to control the project.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 這筆捐款看來出於善意，但卻讓較大的公司取得足夠影響力去控制項目。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: What seemed to be a kind donation became a Trojan horse that allowed the larger company to control the project.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 表面出於善意的捐款，最後成了讓較大公司控制項目的隱藏手段。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The newspaper said the plan appeared to support local businesses but was really intended to make small shops close.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 報章表示，這項計劃表面上支持本地商戶，但真正目的卻是令小店結業。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The newspaper called the plan a Trojan horse designed to close small shops.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 報章形容這項計劃是企圖令小店結業的隱藏手段。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Describe this type of hidden threat in one sentence: It does not attack openly. It first gains trust and then causes harm from inside the group.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 用一句話形容這種隱藏威脅： 它不會公開攻擊，而是先取得信任，然後從團體內部造成破壞。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: A Trojan horse does not attack openly; it gains trust before causing harm from within.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 這種內部威脅不會公開攻擊，而是先取得信任，然後才從內部造成破壞。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The new rule was presented as a harmless change, but it quietly reduced how much influence workers had.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 新規則被說成是一項無害的改動，但其實暗中減少了員工的發言權。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Rather than a harmless change, the new rule was a Trojan horse that quietly reduced workers’ say.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 新規則並非無害改動，而是一項暗中削弱員工發言權的安排。

dossiers.meaningEn: When two or more people put their heads together, they share ideas, discuss a question or plan something together, usually in order to solve a problem or make a decision.
dossiers.meaningZh: 當兩人或以上 put their heads together，意思是他們一起分享想法、討論問題或制訂計劃，通常是為了解決問題或作出決定。
dossiers.registerContextEn: In highly formal academic, legal or technical writing, expressions such as discuss the matter jointly, consult one another or work collaboratively may sometimes be more suitable.
dossiers.registerContextZh: Put your heads together 屬於非正式至中性用語，適合用於日常對話、課堂、團隊會議、家庭討論、工作溝通、社區活動及一般文章。
dossiers.memoryEn: Several heads represent several minds: when the heads come together, the ideas come together.
dossiers.memoryZh: 幾個頭代表幾個人的思想；大家把「頭腦」集合起來，便能把想法集合起來。

semanticRules.titleEn: Normally Use the Expression for Two or More People
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則一：通常用於兩人或以上
semanticRules.en: The idiom describes collective thinking. One person acting completely alone cannot normally put heads together.
semanticRules.zh: 兩名學生共同想辦法。 我們的團隊一起集思廣益。 這個慣用語表示集體思考。 一個人完全獨自思考時，通常不能使用這個表達。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Remove “Together”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：不能刪去 together
semanticRules.en: Do Not Remove “Together”
semanticRules.zh: 不能刪去 together

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Replace “Heads” with “Minds” in This Exercise
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：本練習不能以 minds 取代 heads
semanticRules.en: Do Not Replace “Heads” with “Minds” in This Exercise
semanticRules.zh: 本練習不能以 minds 取代 heads

semanticRules.titleEn: “And + Result” Is Optional
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：and + 結果是可選延伸
semanticRules.en: The words and found a solution are not part of the idiom.
semanticRules.zh: 並非慣用語的一部分。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It Merely Because People Are Physically Close
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：不能只因人們靠得很近便使用
semanticRules.en: The exercise tests only the figurative meaning.
semanticRules.zh: 孩子們拍照時把頭靠在一起。 孩子們集思廣益，解開謎題。 本練習只測試比喻意思。

semanticRules.titleEn: The People Must Share Ideas or Think Together
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：參與者必須分享想法或共同思考
semanticRules.en: They may be sitting together without discussing anything.
semanticRules.zh: 四名學生坐在同一張桌子旁，不代表他們正在共同思考。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Two pupils shared their ideas and found the missing number together.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 兩名學生分享彼此的想法，一起找出了缺少的數字。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The two pupils put their heads together and found the missing number.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 兩名學生集思廣益，找出了缺少的數字。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The nurse and receptionist worked with the booking team to find ways to reduce waiting time.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 護士和接待員與預約團隊共同商量，找出縮短等候時間的方法。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The nurse and receptionist put their heads together with the booking team to reduce waiting time.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 護士和接待員與預約團隊集思廣益，以縮短等候時間。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Before we spend more money, we should discuss what we already have.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 在花更多錢之前，我們應先一起看看現有的物品。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Before we spend more money, let’s put our heads together and see what we already have.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 在花更多錢之前，讓我們先集思廣益，看看現有的物品。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The family discussed the choices for half an hour and then chose a smaller flat.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 這家人一起討論了半小時，然後選擇了一個較小的單位。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: After putting their heads together for half an hour, the family chose a smaller flat.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 這家人集思廣益半小時後，選擇了一個較小的單位。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: We do not know how to fit all the chairs into the room. B: Let us draw a floor plan together.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：我們不知道怎樣把所有椅子放進房間。 乙：讓我們一起畫一張平面圖吧。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Let’s put our heads together and draw a floor plan.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 讓我們集思廣益，一起畫一張平面圖。

dossiers.meaningEn: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.
dossiers.meaningZh: 向對某個範疇有豐富知識或經驗的人請教，以取得有用的資料、意見、建議或想法。
dossiers.registerContextEn: conversations between friends or colleagues; workplace discussions; messages and informal emails; meetings and workshops; conversations with teachers, advisers or experienced relatives.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達屬於非正式語域，特別適合朋友、同事、老師、顧問或家人之間的對話。
dossiers.memoryEn: Imagine selecting useful ideas from a person’s store of knowledge—not touching a real brain.
dossiers.memoryZh: 想像你正在從一個人的知識庫中挑選有用想法，而不是真正接觸大腦。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Other Person Should Have Useful Knowledge
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四：對方應具備有用的知識或經驗
semanticRules.en: If Daniel has no relevant knowledge, the situation does not naturally license the idiom.
semanticRules.zh: 丹尼爾有多年維修單車的經驗，所以我向他請教煞車問題。 如果丹尼爾沒有相關知識，這個情境便不適合使用該慣用語。

semanticRules.titleEn: It Means Asking for Knowledge, Not Copying
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：意思是請教，不是抄襲
semanticRules.en: Work; secretly copying somebody’s homework; stealing a completed report; taking somebody’s private files; forcing somebody to reveal confidential information.
semanticRules.zh: 它通常不表示偷偷抄功課、偷取報告、拿走私人檔案或強迫別人洩露機密。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Interpret the Expression Literally
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：不要按字面理解
semanticRules.en: The idiom does not describe physically touching, opening or removing a brain. It refers figuratively to obtaining useful knowledge through conversation.
semanticRules.zh: 這個慣用語不是指真正接觸、打開或取出人的大腦。 它以比喻方式表示透過交談取得有用知識。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Add Unnecessary Repetition
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：不要加入不必要的意思重複
semanticRules.en: The second clause repeats the meaning already expressed by the idiom.
semanticRules.zh: 第二個分句重複了慣用語已經表達的意思。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with Other “Brain”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：不要與其他包含 Brain 的表達混淆
semanticRules.en: Expressions rack one’s brains be the brains behind something These expressions have different meanings and grammar.
semanticRules.zh: 不要與其他包含 Brain 的表達混淆 pick someone’s brains 向某人請教努力思考或回想 be the brains behind something 是某項計劃背後的主要策劃者這些表達的意思及句法均不相同。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Olivia knows a great deal about indoor plants. I asked her why mine were dying.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 奧莉花對室內植物十分熟悉。我向她請教自己的植物為甚麼正在枯萎。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I picked Olivia’s brains about why my plants were dying.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我向奧莉花請教自己的植物為甚麼正在枯萎。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: My cousin has travelled alone many times. Asking her for advice helped me plan my first solo trip.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 我的表姐多次獨自旅行。向她請教有助我規劃第一次獨遊。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Picking my cousin’s brains helped me plan my first trip alone.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 向表姐請教有助我規劃第一次獨遊。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: We need some ideas for our new podcast. B: Marco produces one every week. We could ask him how he plans it.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：我們的新網上節目需要一些想法。 乙：馬高每星期都製作一個節目。我們可以向他請教如何規劃。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: We could pick Marco’s brains about planning the podcast.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我們可以向馬高請教如何規劃網上節目。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The retired engineer explained the machine for an hour. Her explanation gave the student the idea she needed.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 退休工程師用了一小時解釋那部機器。她的解釋令學生取得所需想法。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: She got the idea after spending an hour picking the retired engineer’s brains.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 她花了一小時向退休工程師請教後，取得了所需想法。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: I cannot decide which course to take. B: Our tutor has studied both subjects. Let us ask her before deciding.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：我無法決定修讀哪個課程。 乙：我們的導師修讀過兩個科目。讓我們在決定前向她請教。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Before choosing a course, let’s pick our tutor’s brains.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 選擇課程前，讓我們向導師請教。

dossiers.meaningEn: to pass the worst stage of a difficult situation and begin to improve
dossiers.meaningZh: 渡過最艱難的階段，並開始好轉。
dossiers.registerContextEn: The expression often carries a hopeful or relieved tone. It may also be used cautiously with may, might, could, seem or appear when the improvement is not yet certain. Dictionaries illustrate it with people, illnesses, businesses and wider situations.
dossiers.registerContextZh: Turn the corner 屬於中性表達，適用範圍廣泛。
dossiers.memoryEn: Before the corner, the difficult road continues; after turning it, the journey begins moving in a better direction.
dossiers.memoryZh: 繞過街角前，困難的道路仍在延續；繞過街角後，旅程開始朝更好的方向前進。

semanticRules.titleEn: It Means “Begin to Improve”, Not “Become Perfect”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則二：表示「開始好轉」，而不是「變得完美」
semanticRules.en: The patient is still weak, but her condition has begun to improve. The idiom does not automatically mean complete recovery.
semanticRules.zh: 病人已渡過最危險的階段。 這個慣用語並不自動表示病人已經完全康復。

semanticRules.titleEn: There Must Be a Difficult Earlier Period
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則三：此前必須有一段困難時期
semanticRules.en: Natural: Nothing establishes an earlier difficult period.
semanticRules.zh: 店舖在虧損數月後開始走出低谷。 句子沒有交代此前曾經歷任何困難，因此不適合使用這個慣用語。

semanticRules.titleEn: One Good Result May Not Be Enough
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：一次好結果未必足夠
semanticRules.en: The business may be turning the corner, but one good week is not enough to be certain.
semanticRules.zh: 一次較好的表現未必足以證明長期問題已真正改善。 這種情況應使用較審慎的語氣。

semanticRules.titleEn: Avoid Accidental Literal Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：避免意外使用字面意思
semanticRules.en: Literal: Idiomatic:
semanticRules.zh: 司機駛過街角，在銀行外停下。 經過數月銷售低迷後，這盤生意開始走出低谷。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Idiom’s Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：不要重複慣用語已表達的意思
semanticRules.en: After a difficult start, the team turned the corner.
semanticRules.zh: 慣用語本身已經表達「渡過困難階段並開始好轉」，不應在後面立即重複同一意思。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The shop lost money for several weeks, but it has now begun to make a profit.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 店舖連續數星期虧損，但現在已開始錄得利潤。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: After several bad weeks, the shop has finally turned the corner.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 經過數星期的困難後，店舖終於開始走出低谷。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The class had received low marks for months. The new teacher introduced shorter practice sessions, and the results began to improve.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 全班連續數月取得低分。新老師引入較短的練習時段後，成績開始改善。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The new teacher helped the class turn the corner with shorter practice sessions.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 新老師透過較短的練習時段，幫助全班開始取得改善。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: The patient is showing some improvement, but she is still in a serious condition. B: Ask the doctor whether she has passed the most dangerous stage.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：病人的情況有所改善，但病情仍然嚴重。 乙：問問醫生她是否已渡過最危險的階段。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Has the patient turned the corner, or is she still in danger?
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 病人是否已渡過最危險的階段，還是仍然有危險？

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Aaron has struggled with English for a long time. Continuing the same study routine may allow him to begin making real progress.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: Aaron 學習英語已經困難了一段很長時間。繼續保持相同的溫習習慣，可能令他開始取得真正進步。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: By keeping the same study routine, Aaron may be able to turn the corner in English.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: Aaron 持續保持相同的溫習習慣，可能有助他在英語方面開始取得真正進步。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The project had been delayed because important parts were missing. Once the parts arrived, the work began moving forward steadily.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 項目因欠缺重要零件而延誤。零件送到後，工程開始穩定地向前推進。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The project began to turn the corner once the missing parts arrived.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 欠缺的零件送到後，項目開始走出困境。

dossiers.lemma: have your heart in your mouth
dossiers.sourcePdf: Idiom 92 - 「HAVE YOUR HEART IN YOUR MOUTH」.pdf
dossiers.meaningEn: To have your heart in your mouth means to feel extremely nervous or frightened, especially while facing danger, waiting for an important result or watching something whose outcome is uncertain.
dossiers.meaningZh: have your heart in your mouth 表示極度緊張、害怕或提心吊膽，尤其用於面對危險、等候重要結果，或觀看結果未明的事情。
dossiers.registerContextEn: 1. everyday conversation; 2. personal stories; 3. interviews; 4. sports reports; 5. films and fiction; 6. less formal journalism.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個慣用語主要屬於非正式至中性用語，自然用於日常對話、個人故事、訪問、體育報道、電影、 小說及較不正式的新聞寫作。
dossiers.fixed: have one’s heart in one’s mouth
surfaceForms: My heart was in my mouth
had his heart in his mouth
Eva’s heart was in her mouth
had my heart in my mouth
boy’s heart was in his mouth
Our hearts were in our mouths
dossiers.memoryEn: When fear makes your heart pound upwards, imagine it rising towards your mouth.
dossiers.memoryZh: 當恐懼令心臟猛烈跳動時，可以想像它正在向口腔方向升上去。

semanticRules.titleEn: Match both possessives
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則一：兩個所有格必須配合
semanticRules.en: Match both possessives
semanticRules.zh: 兩個所有格必須配合

semanticRules.titleEn: “Have” and “be” are both central
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則三：have 和 be 都是核心句式
semanticRules.en: “Have” and “be” are both central
semanticRules.zh: have 和 be 都是核心句式

semanticRules.titleEn: Do not repeat the same meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：不要重複同一意思
semanticRules.en: Do not repeat the same meaning
semanticRules.zh: 不要重複同一意思

semanticRules.titleEn: Do not interpret the expression literally
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：不要按字面理解
semanticRules.en: The idiom does not mean that the physical heart has moved into the mouth.
semanticRules.zh: 這個慣用語並不是說心臟真的移到口腔內。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do not confuse it with other “heart” idioms
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：不要與其他 heart 慣用語混淆
semanticRules.en: Your heart is in the right place. Your heart sinks.
semanticRules.zh: 你的出發點是好的。 你突然感到失望或沮喪。 你感到極度緊張或害怕。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do not overuse “when”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十三：不要過度使用 when
semanticRules.en: Do not overuse “when”
semanticRules.zh: 不要過度使用 when

candidateQuestions.promptEn: I felt extremely nervous as I opened the email containing my exam results.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 我打開載有考試成績的電郵時，感到極度緊張。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: My heart was in my mouth as I opened the email containing my exam results.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我打開載有考試成績的電郵時，緊張得心也快要跳出來。
candidateQuestions.highlight: My heart was in my mouth

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The football fans watched in extreme nervousness as the ball flew towards the empty goal.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 足球飛向空門時，球迷極度緊張地觀看。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The football fans had their hearts in their mouths as the ball flew towards the empty goal.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 足球飛向空門時，球迷都緊張得心也快要跳出來。
candidateQuestions.highlight: had their hearts in their mouths

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Why are you shaking? B: A car nearly hit the cyclist in front of me.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：你為甚麼在發抖？ 乙：一輛汽車剛才差點撞到我前面的單車手。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: My heart was in my mouth when the car nearly hit the cyclist in front of me.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 那輛汽車差點撞到我前面的單車手時，我嚇得心也快要跳出來。
candidateQuestions.highlight: My heart was in my mouth

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The passengers sat in great fear as smoke came from the engine.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 引擎冒煙時，乘客非常害怕地坐着。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The passengers sat with their hearts in their mouths as smoke came from the engine.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 引擎冒煙時，乘客提心吊膽地坐着。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Because the road was covered in ice, we were terrified as we drove down the hill.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 由於路面結冰，我們駕車下山時非常害怕。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Because the road was covered in ice, we drove down the hill with our hearts in our mouths.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 由於路面結冰，我們駕車下山時都提心吊膽。

dossiers.meaningEn: If somebody is not just a pretty face, they are attractive but also intelligent, talented, skilled, capable or valuable in another important way.
dossiers.meaningZh: 如果某人 is not just a pretty face，意思是這個人不但外表吸引，還有才智、才能、技術、能力或其他重要優點。
dossiers.registerContextEn: informal speeches; light-hearted introductions.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達屬於非正式及幽默語域，尤其適合用於：
surfaceForms: not be just a pretty face
dossiers.memoryEn: The appearance may attract attention first, but the person has much more to offer.
dossiers.memoryZh: 外表可能首先吸引注意，但這個人真正擁有的遠不止外表。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Source Must Establish an Appearance Contrast
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：原句必須建立外表與能力之間的對比
semanticRules.en: The second source says nothing about appearance or an appearance-based assumption. The idiom would therefore be unsupported.
semanticRules.zh: 第二個原句沒有提及外表，也沒有建立任何以貌取人的假設，因此不足以支持這個慣用語。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It Merely to Mean “Intelligent”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：不要把它當作 intelligent 的普通同義詞
semanticRules.en: 1. the person is attractive or is being judged mainly by appearance; 2. the person also has meaningful intelligence, talent or ability.
semanticRules.zh: 這個表達結合兩個意思：

semanticRules.titleEn: Men and Women Can Both Be Described This Way
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：男女均可使用這個表達
semanticRules.en: The idiom may be used about any gender. When used about a man, pretty often sounds deliberately playful. However, appropriateness depends on the relationship and context—not merely on grammatical correctness.
semanticRules.zh: 這個慣用語可以形容任何性別。 形容男性時，pretty 通常會帶有刻意的玩笑語氣。 不過，用法是否合適取決於人物關係及語境，而不只是文法是否正確。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Same Meaning Mechanically
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：不要機械式重複相同意思
semanticRules.en: The second clause supplies a specific independent ability.
semanticRules.zh: 較佳的句子以具體能力補充資料，而不是再次解釋慣用語本身。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use “Pretty Face” Literally
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：不要使用字面意思
semanticRules.en: The drawing shows a pretty face.
semanticRules.zh: 這幅畫展示了一張漂亮的臉。 這名設計師並非徒有其表； 整個系列都是由她創作的。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Ava is often praised for her looks, but she can also solve difficult maths problems.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 艾娃經常因外表受到稱讚，但她也能解答困難的數學問題。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Ava is not just a pretty face; she can also solve difficult maths problems.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 艾娃並非徒有其表；她也能解答困難的數學問題。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Owen wants people to judge him for more than his appearance because he has years of nursing experience.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 歐文希望大家不要只按外表評價他，因為他擁有多年護理經驗。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Owen wants people to understand that he is not just a pretty face; he has years of nursing experience.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 歐文希望大家明白他並非只有外表；他擁有多年護理經驗。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The players thought the new coach had been hired mainly because he looked good in publicity photographs. His clever training plan changed their minds.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 球員以為新教練主要因為宣傳照片中的外表吸引而獲聘。他聰明的訓練計劃改變了他們的看法。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The players discovered that the new coach was not just a pretty face when they saw his clever training plan.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 球員看到新教練聰明的訓練計劃後，發現他不只是外表俊俏。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: You cooked all this food? B: Yes. Why do you look so surprised?
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：所有食物都是你煮的嗎？ 乙：是的。你為甚麼看來那麼驚訝？
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Don’t look so shocked. I’m not just a pretty face—I can cook too.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 不要那麼驚訝。我可不只是外表好看——我也懂得烹飪。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A profile of Jay explained that he was attractive, thoughtful and able to write very well.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 一篇有關傑伊的人物介紹指出，他不但外表吸引，而且思想細膩，寫作能力也十分出色。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The article presented Jay as someone who was not just a pretty face but also a thoughtful writer.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 文章把傑伊描寫成一個不只有吸引外表、同時也是思想細膩作家的人。

dossiers.meaningEn: to make a foolish or avoidable mistake that causes embarrassment or failure
dossiers.meaningZh: 犯下愚蠢或本可避免的錯誤，因而出醜或失敗。
dossiers.registerContextEn: The expression is mainly British, informal and especially common in journalism, sport and public commentary. Oxford describes banana skin as British and informal, while Collins notes that the figurative use is mainly British and journalistic.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達主要屬英式英語，語氣較口語化，尤其常見於新聞、體育報道及對公眾人物的評論。
dossiers.memoryEn: A tiny banana skin can bring down a confident walker; one tiny mistake can bring down a confident person or team.
dossiers.memoryZh: 一塊小小的香蕉皮可以令自信的行人跌倒；一個小小的錯誤也可以令自信的人或團隊失手。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use the Figurative Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則一：使用比喻意思
semanticRules.en: Daniel stepped on a real banana skin and fell.
semanticRules.zh: 踏中真正的香蕉皮而跌倒。 Daniel 在訪問中說錯公司名稱，因低級錯誤而出醜。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Mistake Should Be Embarrassing or Damaging
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則二：錯誤應帶來尷尬或麻煩
semanticRules.en: The presenter showed the wrong figures in front of the directors. The presenter dropped a pencil but immediately picked it up.
semanticRules.zh: 主持人在董事面前展示了錯誤數字。 主持人掉下一枝鉛筆，但立即把它撿起。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Error Is Often Avoidable
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則三：錯誤通常本可避免
semanticRules.en: The Error Is Often Avoidable
semanticRules.zh: 錯誤通常本可避免

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Every Failure
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：不要用來形容所有失敗
semanticRules.en: The clear favourite lost because it ignored a basic rule. The weaker team played brilliantly and narrowly defeated an equally strong opponent.
semanticRules.zh: 大熱門因忽略基本規則而落敗。 實力較弱的球隊有出色表現，僅以些微差距擊敗實力相若的對手。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Idiom’s Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：不要重複解釋慣用語意思
semanticRules.en: Do Not Repeat the Idiom’s Meaning
semanticRules.zh: 不要重複解釋慣用語意思

candidateQuestions.promptEn: At the company meeting, the presenter showed last year’s sales figures instead of this year’s figures, making her look unprepared.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 在公司會議上，主持人展示了去年的銷售數字，而不是今年的數字，令自己顯得毫無準備。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: At the company meeting, the presenter slipped on a banana skin by showing last year’s sales figures.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 主持人在公司會議上展示去年的銷售數字，因低級錯誤而出醜。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The captain has returned, and the team has carefully studied the opponent. An unexpected foolish defeat is now less likely.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 隊長已經歸隊，而且球隊已仔細研究對手。現在因低級錯誤而意外落敗的可能性較低。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Now that the captain is back, the team is unlikely to slip on a banana skin against this opponent.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 隊長歸隊後，球隊不大可能在面對這個對手時意外失手。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The teacher warned that forgetting to write the class name on the project could lead to an embarrassing loss of marks.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 老師警告，忘記在專題習作上寫上班別，可能會令人尷尬地失去分數。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The teacher warned that the class could slip on a banana skin over one missing name on the project.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 老師警告，全班可能只因專題習作上少了一個名稱而尷尬失分。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: We only had to book the hall for Friday. Why was the event cancelled? B: The club booked it for Thursday by mistake.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：我們只需要預訂星期五的禮堂。為甚麼活動被取消了？ 乙：會所錯誤預訂了星期四。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: “How did the club manage to slip on a banana skin over such a simple booking?” the organiser asked.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 主辦者問：「會所怎會在如此簡單的預訂上犯下低級錯誤？」

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The bank is launching a new app, but one simple error in the payment dates could cause public embarrassment.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 銀行即將推出新的應用程式，但付款日期上的一個簡單錯誤可能會令銀行公開出醜。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: There is a real risk that the bank will slip on a banana skin when it launches the new app.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 銀行推出新應用程式時，確實有可能因低級錯誤而出醜。

dossiers.meaningEn: A person who has a supporting or less important role beside someone who receives more attention, authority or recognition.
dossiers.meaningZh: 在另一位較受重視、較有權力或較受注目的人身邊，擔任配角、輔助角色或處於次要地位的人。
dossiers.registerContextEn: Second banana is informal and mainly American. Dictionaries label it informal, slang or chiefly American, although it is widely understandable through films, television, sport and entertainment writing.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 它是偏美式的非正式用語，在電影、電視、體育及娛樂文章中頗常見。 雖然不少英語使用者都能理解，但在英式英語中，second fiddle 有時會較常見。
dossiers.memoryEn: The top banana is the star; the second banana stands beside the star in the supporting position.
dossiers.memoryZh: Top banana 是主角；second banana 則站在主角身邊擔任配角。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do not translate it literally
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則二：不可按字面翻譯
semanticRules.en: Incorrect idiomatic translation: Natural translations:
semanticRules.zh: 第二隻香蕉配角第二號人物次要人物陪襯角色

semanticRules.titleEn: Use “to” to identify the leading person
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：使用 to 指出主要人物
semanticRules.en: With may suggest partnership, but it does not clearly show who occupies the more important position.
semanticRules.zh: With 可能只表示合作，並沒有清楚指出誰的地位較重要。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do not use it merely for “second place”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：不可只因某人排名第二而使用
semanticRules.en: The race result does not create a supporting relationship between Ben and the winner.
semanticRules.zh: 比賽名次並沒有建立本與冠軍之間的配角關係。 本在體育節目中擔任第二號人物，因為主要主持得到差不多所有關注。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do not assume every assistant is a second banana
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：不要把每個助手都視為配角
semanticRules.en: An assistant may have an equal, independent or highly important role. Use second banana only when the context establishes that one person is clearly less prominent or less important than another.
semanticRules.zh: 助手可能擁有平等、獨立或十分重要的角色。 只有當語境清楚表示某人較不受注目或地位較次要時，才應使用 second banana。

semanticRules.titleEn: Keep the human-role meaning clear
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：清楚建立人物角色的意思
semanticRules.en: This does not show that either person was more important. This clearly licenses second banana.
semanticRules.zh: 亞歷克斯站在本身邊，並不代表其中一人較重要。 本是喜劇表演的主角，而亞歷克斯擔任配角。 這個語境清楚支持使用 second banana。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do not repeat the idiom’s meaning unnecessarily
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：不要不必要地重複慣用語的意思
semanticRules.en: The second half merely explains the idiom again. Preparing the situations is a specific task, not merely a repetition of “supporting role”.
semanticRules.zh: 句子後半部分只是在再次解釋慣用語。 亞歷克斯是這個喜劇組合中的配角。 亞歷克斯身為配角，負責為本的笑話鋪排情境。 鋪排情境是一項具體工作，並不只是重複「擔任配角」。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Ben was the star of the comedy duo. Alex had the supporting role and received less attention.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 本是這個喜劇組合的主角。亞歷克斯擔任配角，得到的關注較少。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: In the comedy duo, Alex was the second banana to Ben.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 在這個喜劇組合中，亞歷克斯是本身邊的配角。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Caleb believed that he and his partner were equal. He later noticed that everyone ignored his ideas and treated his partner as the leader.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 卡萊布原以為自己和拍檔地位平等。後來，他發現所有人都忽略他的想法，並把拍檔視為領導者。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Caleb did not realise that he had become the second banana until everyone began ignoring his ideas.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 直到所有人開始忽略他的想法，卡萊布才發現自己已成為配角。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Chloe understands the topic better than Peter. Peter is therefore happy to support her and let her lead the presentation.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 克洛伊比彼得更熟悉這個題目。因此，彼得樂意協助她，並讓她帶領簡報。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Peter was willing to play second banana to Chloe because she understood the topic better.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 彼得願意在克洛伊身邊擔任配角，因為她更熟悉這個題目。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Olivia had worked under her older brother in the family business for years. She now wanted the power to make her own decisions.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 奧利維亞多年來一直在家族生意中協助哥哥。她現在希望有權自行作出決定。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Olivia was no longer willing to remain the second banana in the family business.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 奧利維亞不再願意繼續擔任家族生意中的次要人物。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The production team needed someone who could organise the details while the main presenter led the meetings and appeared on camera.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 製作團隊需要一個能夠整理細節的人，而主要主持則負責帶領會議及在鏡頭前出現。
