candidateQuestions.answerEn: The production team wanted a second banana who could organise the details while the main presenter led the meetings.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 製作團隊需要一位能夠整理細節的配角，而主要主持則負責帶領會議。

dossiers.meaningEn: A person or animal that is extremely thin, often to the point that their bones appear clearly visible.
dossiers.meaningZh: 一個瘦骨嶙峋的人或動物；瘦得全身骨頭清晰可見，彷彿只剩下皮和骨頭。
dossiers.registerContextEn: The expression is informal and very strong.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達屬於非正式用語，而且語氣十分強烈。
dossiers.memoryEn: Imagine a body with so little flesh that it seems to be only a bag holding bones.
dossiers.memoryZh: 想像一個幾乎沒有肌肉的身體，彷彿只是一個裝着骨頭的袋。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use It Only for Extreme Thinness
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四：只用於極度消瘦
semanticRules.en: The idiom is much stronger than slim or thin.
semanticRules.zh: 那隻獲救的狗瘦得每根肋骨都清晰可見。 這個慣用語的程度遠強於 slim 或 thin。

semanticRules.titleEn: People and Animals Are Both Possible
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：人和動物都可以使用
semanticRules.en: People and Animals Are Both Possible
semanticRules.zh: 病後，他看起來瘦得只剩皮包骨。 那匹獲救的馬瘦骨嶙峋。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Add a Second Explanation
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：不要再次解釋相同意思
semanticRules.en: The second part largely repeats the meaning of the idiom. The visible ribs provide evidence that licenses the idiom rather than repeating it afterwards.
semanticRules.zh: 後半部分大致上重複了慣用語的意思。 肋骨清晰可見是支持使用這個慣用語的證據，而不是在慣用語之後再次解釋。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It as a Medical Diagnosis
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：不要把它當作醫療診斷
semanticRules.en: The idiom is not precise clinical language.
semanticRules.zh: 這個慣用語並不是準確的臨床用語。

semanticRules.titleEn: Avoid Direct Personal Insults
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：避免直接侮辱別人
semanticRules.en: Avoid Direct Personal Insults
semanticRules.zh: 他的家人十分擔心，因為他病後瘦得只剩皮包骨。

semanticRules.titleEn: Avoid Literal Contexts
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：避免字面語境
semanticRules.en: The neglected horse had become a bag of bones.
semanticRules.zh: 本練習中的所有答案都必須使用比喻意思。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The rescued dog was extremely thin when it arrived at the animal home.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 那隻獲救的狗抵達動物之家時極度消瘦。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: When it arrived at the animal home, the rescued dog was a bag of bones.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 那隻獲救的狗抵達動物之家時瘦得只剩皮包骨。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Simon had lost so much weight that he no longer resembled the lively teacher his friends knew.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 西蒙消瘦了很多，已不像朋友所熟悉的那名充滿活力的老師。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: After losing so much weight, Simon seemed more like a bag of bones than the lively teacher his friends knew.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 西蒙大幅消瘦後，看起來與其說是朋友熟悉的活潑老師，不如說是瘦得只剩皮包骨。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The poor horse had almost no flesh on its body, and it could barely stand.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 那匹可憐的馬身上幾乎沒有肉，而且勉強才能站立。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Little more than a bag of bones, the poor horse could barely stand.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 那匹可憐的馬瘦得幾乎只剩下骨頭，勉強才能站立。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: After weeks without enough food, the rescued man was far thinner than the word slim would suggest.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 幾星期缺乏足夠食物後，那名獲救男子的消瘦程度遠超過 slim 所能表達。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: After weeks without enough food, the rescued man was not merely slim; he was a bag of bones.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 幾星期缺乏足夠食物後，那名獲救男子並不只是纖瘦，而是瘦得只剩皮包骨。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Every rib on the stray dog was clearly visible.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 那隻流浪狗的每根肋骨都清晰可見。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: With every rib showing, the stray dog was clearly a bag of bones.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 那隻流浪狗的每根肋骨都清晰可見，明顯已經瘦得只剩皮包骨。

dossiers.meaningEn: If someone or something is back to square one, an earlier attempt has failed or previous progress has been lost, so the work must begin again from the starting point.
dossiers.meaningZh: 如果某人或某件事 back to square one，意思是之前的嘗試失敗了，或先前的進展已經失去，因此必須回到起點重新開始。
dossiers.registerContextEn: frustration; disappointment; resignation; warning; determination to begin again.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 它可以表達挫折、失望、無奈、警告，或重新開始的決心。
dossiers.memoryEn: You moved across the board, but one setback sent you back to the first square.
dossiers.memoryZh: 你原本已在棋盤上向前移動，但一次挫折把你送回第一格。

semanticRules.titleEn: Earlier Progress Must Have Existed
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則一：之前必須已有進展
semanticRules.en: Earlier Progress Must Have Existed
semanticRules.zh: 我們幾乎完成了報告，但檔案被刪除了。 我們回到了原點。 今天是我們第一天開始報告，所以我們回到了原點。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Setback Must Be Major Enough
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則二：挫折必須嚴重得足以令工作重做
semanticRules.en: Every page of the report was lost. One comma in the report is wrong.
semanticRules.zh: 報告的每一頁都遺失了。 團隊回到原點了。 報告中有一個逗號用錯了。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：不要重複慣用語已表達的意思
semanticRules.en: Do Not Repeat the Meaning
semanticRules.zh: 我們回到原點，所以必須把一切重新從頭開始。 這個項目令我們回到原點。

semanticRules.titleEn: “Back at Square One” Is Not This Exercise’s Target
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九
semanticRules.en: Back at square one is used naturally in English, but this set trains one exact target. Do not replace to with at in the answers.
semanticRules.zh: back at square one 不是本練習的目標 back at square one 在英語中屬於自然用法，但本練習只訓練一個確切形式。 答案中不可把 to 改成 at。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use It Naturally, Not for Every Restart
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：自然使用，不是每次重新開始都適合
semanticRules.en: Back to square one usually carries the idea of lost progress, failure or serious frustration. For a normal planned restart, start again or repeat may be more suitable.
semanticRules.zh: back to square one 通常帶有失去進展、失敗或嚴重挫折的意思。 若只是按照計劃正常重做，使用 start again 或 repeat 可能更合適。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The final poster file was lost, so all our design work must begin again.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 最後的海報檔案遺失了，因此我們所有設計工作都必須重新開始。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: We are back to square one with the poster because the final file was lost.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 由於最後的檔案遺失了，我們的海報設計工作回到原點。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: If the new evidence is false, the police may lose every useful lead and have to restart their search.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 如果新證據是假的，警方可能會失去所有有用線索，並要重新展開搜索。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: If the new evidence is false, the police could be back to square one in their search.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 如果新證據是假的，警方的搜索工作可能會回到原點。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The small first test was supposed to move the plan forward. Instead, it showed that the plan’s basic idea was wrong and that the entire plan had to be reconsidered.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 這次小型初步測試原本應推動計劃向前。相反，它顯示計劃的基本構思有誤，整個計劃都需要重新考慮。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The small first test was meant to move the plan forward, but instead it put us back to square one with the plan.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 小型初步測試原本應推動計劃向前，卻反而令整個計劃回到原點。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: If the shop cannot make the chosen parts, we may need to redesign the model from the beginning.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 如果店舖無法製造我們選擇的零件，我們可能需要從頭重新設計模型。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: We may have to go back to square one with the model if the shop cannot make the parts we chose.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 如果店舖無法製造我們選擇的零件，我們可能需要從頭重新設計模型。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The two sides had agreed on almost every price. One unclear sentence then caused both sides to withdraw everything they had accepted.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 雙方幾乎已同意所有價格。其後，一句意思不清的句子令雙方撤回所有已接受的內容。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: One unclear sentence brought both sides back to square one in their price talks.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 一句意思不清的句子令雙方的價格商討回到原點。

dossiers.meaningEn: A general view or understanding of a whole subject, situation, system or activity, without concentrating on every small detail.
dossiers.meaningZh: 對整個主題、情況、制度或活動的整體概覽，而不集中於每一項細節。
dossiers.registerContextEn: conversation; lessons and presentations; reports and articles; workplace communication; project discussions; explanations of systems or processes.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 它可用於口語及書面英語。 當說話者希望先清楚整理整體資料，再進入細節時，這個表達尤其有用。
dossiers.memoryEn: A bird sees the whole area from above; a bird’s-eye view helps you see the whole subject before studying its smaller parts.
dossiers.memoryZh: 飛鳥從高處看見整片地方；a bird’s-eye view 則幫助你先掌握整個主題，再研究較小的部分。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use “Of” Only When Needed
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則三：按需要使用 of
semanticRules.en: Use “Of” Only When Needed
semanticRules.zh: 按需要使用 of

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：不要重複相同意思
semanticRules.en: The report gives a bird’s-eye view of the project.
semanticRules.zh: 使用目標表達後，不要立即再以另一個子句重複「提供整體概覽」的意思。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for One Small Detail
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：不要用來描述單一小細節
semanticRules.en: Do Not Use It for One Small Detail
semanticRules.zh: 一份報告概括說明全班主要的語言問題。

semanticRules.titleEn: It Is Not an Opinion
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：它不等於個人意見
semanticRules.en: my opinion; my belief; my personal preference; one side of an argument.
semanticRules.zh: a bird’s-eye view 表示整體概覽，並不單純表示個人意見或立場。

semanticRules.titleEn: It Does Not Promise Every Detail
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：它不代表包括所有細節
semanticRules.en: It Does Not Promise Every Detail
semanticRules.zh: 它不代表包括所有細節

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The first page shows readers the main parts of the project without explaining every detail.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 第一頁向讀者展示項目的主要部分，但沒有解釋所有細節。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The first page gives readers a bird’s-eye view of the project.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 第一頁讓讀者掌握整個項目的概況。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Before choosing a date for the event, the organisers looked at the whole schedule rather than one individual activity.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 在選擇活動日期前，主辦人員查看了整個時間表，而不是只看其中一項活動。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Before choosing a date, the organisers got a bird’s-eye view of the whole schedule.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 選擇日期前，主辦人員先掌握了整個時間表的全貌。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The team asked the manager to give them a broad explanation of the new plan.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 團隊請經理向他們概括解釋新計劃。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The team asked the manager for a bird’s-eye view of the new plan.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 團隊請經理概括說明新計劃的全貌。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: I would like a general picture of the company before reading all its reports.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 我想在閱讀公司的所有報告前，先了解公司的整體情況。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I would like a bird’s-eye view of the company before reading all its reports.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我想在閱讀公司的所有報告前，先了解公司的整體情況。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: I understand each task, but I cannot see how the tasks are connected. B: Look at the wall chart.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：我明白每項工作，但看不出這些工作如何互相連繫。 乙：看看牆上的圖表。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: If you need a bird’s-eye view of how the tasks are connected, look at the wall chart.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 如果你需要了解各項工作如何互相連繫，請查看牆上的圖表。

dossiers.meaningEn: To spend time recovering your strength, confidence or happiness after a defeat, disappointment, failure or other upsetting experience.
dossiers.meaningZh: 在失敗、落敗、失望或其他令人難受的經歷後，花時間休整、平復心情或重拾信心。
dossiers.registerContextEn: everyday conversation; sports discussion; news and commentary; workplace conversation; descriptions of personal disappointment; discussions of failed plans or public criticism.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達帶有比喻色彩，語氣一般屬於中性至非正式。 它常見於日常對話、體育評論、新聞報道、 工作場合及描述個人挫敗的語境。
dossiers.memoryEn: The animal withdraws to recover from an injury; the person withdraws to recover from a setback.
dossiers.memoryZh: 動物退下來養傷；人則退下來平復挫敗。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for an Ordinary Rest
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：不要用來表示一般休息
semanticRules.en: The speaker is merely tired. No defeat or upsetting experience has occurred.
semanticRules.zh: 說話者只是疲倦，並沒有經歷失敗或打擊。 我的建議被拒，因此我會回家休整一下。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with Physical Treatment
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：不要與真正的傷口處理混淆
semanticRules.en: The injured dog licked its wound.
semanticRules.zh: 受傷的狗舔自己的傷口。 落敗的球隊回家休整。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Idiom’s Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：不要再次解釋相同意思
semanticRules.en: The source explains the recovery. The idiom replaces that explanation.
semanticRules.zh: 原句負責解釋「恢復」； 答案則以慣用語濃縮這個意思，不應再次重複。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use “One’s” in a Normal Personal
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：一般句子中不要直接使用 one’s
semanticRules.en: Do Not Use “One’s” in a Normal Personal
semanticRules.zh: 一般句子中不要直接使用 one’s

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The team lost the final badly and went home to recover from the disappointment.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 球隊在決賽中大敗，之後回家平復失望的情緒。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The team went home to lick its wounds after the heavy defeat.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 球隊慘敗後回家休整，慢慢平復失望。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Why did Sofia cancel dinner? B: She did not get the role and wants to be alone while she gets over the rejection.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：索菲婭為甚麼取消晚餐？ 乙：她沒有獲得那個角色，想獨處一下，平復被拒的打擊。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: She wants to be alone for a while to lick her wounds after the rejection.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 她被拒後想獨處一會，休整並平復心情。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The bad review left the writer upset and trying to rebuild her confidence.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 那篇負面評論令作家感到難過，需要重新建立信心。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The bad review left the writer licking her wounds.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 那篇負面評論令作家受挫，需要休整並重拾信心。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: After recovering from their first failed attempt, the group tried the project again.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 小組從第一次失敗的嘗試中恢復過來後，再次進行該項目。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: After licking their wounds following their first failed attempt, the group tried the project again.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 小組從第一次失敗的嘗試中休整過來後，再次進行該項目。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: You may feel hurt after the public criticism, but do not spend too long feeling sorry for yourself.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 受到公開批評後，你可能會感到受傷，但不要用太長時間自怨自艾。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: You may need to lick your wounds after the public criticism, but do not spend too long doing so.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 受到公開批評後，你可能需要休整一下，但不要長時間自怨自艾。

dossiers.meaningEn: to behave carefully and avoid unnecessary risk, danger or possible failure
dossiers.meaningZh: 謹慎行事；採取較穩妥的做法；避免不必要的風險、危險或失敗
dossiers.registerContextEn: play it safe is generally informal and is especially natural in conversation, personal messages, interviews and accessible general writing. Cambridge labels the expression informal, while Collins records it in a wide range of ordinary spoken and written contexts.
dossiers.registerContextZh: play it safe 通常屬於非正式表達，特別適合用於：
dossiers.memoryEn: Imagine that a decision is like a move in a game: instead of making the risky move, you choose the safer one.
dossiers.memoryZh: 想像每個決定都像遊戲中的一步：你沒有選擇高風險的一步，而是選擇較穩妥的一步。

semanticRules.titleEn: Inflect “Play”, Not “Safe”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則二：改變 play，不要改變 safe
semanticRules.en: Inflect “Play”, Not “Safe”
semanticRules.zh: 改變 play，不要改變 safe

semanticRules.titleEn: There Must Be a Real Risk or Uncertainty
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四：語境必須存在真正的風險或不確定性
semanticRules.en: There Must Be a Real Risk or Uncertainty
semanticRules.zh: 火車可能會延誤，所以我會提早出發，以策安全。 普通地喝水通常不涉及需要避免的風險。

semanticRules.titleEn: It Does Not Mean “Guarantee Complete Safety”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：它不表示「保證絕對安全」
semanticRules.en: Playing it safe means choosing a cautious option. The result may still be uncertain.
semanticRules.zh: play it safe 表示選擇較謹慎的方案，但結果仍然可能存在不確定性。

semanticRules.titleEn: Avoid Unnecessary Repetition
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：避免重複相同意思
semanticRules.en: The idiom already communicates the idea of avoiding risk.
semanticRules.zh: 慣用語本身已經表達「避免風險」，不需要再次重複解釋。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with Literal Play
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：不要與字面上的 play 混淆
semanticRules.en: The children played safely in the garden.
semanticRules.zh: 孩子們安全地在花園玩耍。 父母穩妥起見，在暴風雨期間讓孩子留在室內。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It Automatically Whenever “Safety” Appears
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：不要在看見「安全」題材時自動使用
semanticRules.en: The expression describes a cautious decision between possible courses of action. It is not merely a general instruction to follow every safety rule.
semanticRules.zh: 這個表達描述的是：當事人在多個做法之間選擇了較謹慎的一個。 它並不單純表示遵守所有安全規則。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The later bus might make me late, so I took the earlier one.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 較遲的巴士可能令我遲到，所以我乘搭了較早的一班。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I played it safe and took the earlier bus.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我為求穩妥，乘搭了較早的一班巴士。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The shop owner orders only a small amount of each new product until she knows whether customers want it.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 店主每次只會少量訂購新產品，直至她知道顧客是否喜歡為止。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The shop owner usually plays it safe with new products and orders only a small amount at first.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 店主處理新產品時通常較為保守，最初只會少量訂購。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The hikers chose the marked path because nobody knew the condition of the other route.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 遠足人士選擇了有標記的路徑，因為沒有人知道另一條路線的情況。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: By choosing the marked path, the hikers played it safe.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 遠足人士選擇有標記的路徑，採取了較穩妥的做法。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: We have chosen the same familiar plan again because we fear making a mistake. B: Are we being sensible, or are we being too cautious?
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：因為害怕犯錯，我們再次選擇了同一個熟悉的方案。 乙：我們是做法明智，還是過分保守？
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Are we playing it safe, or are we being unnecessarily cautious?
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我們是在謹慎行事，還是過分保守？

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The warning light had appeared twice, so I stopped the car.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 警告燈已經亮起兩次，所以我停下了汽車。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I played it safe and stopped the car because the warning light had appeared twice.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 由於警告燈已經亮起兩次，我為免冒險而停下了汽車。

dossiers.meaningEn: A top banana is the most important, powerful or highest-ranking person in a group, organisation or activity.
dossiers.meaningZh: top banana 指一個群體、機構或活動中最重要、最有權力或地位最高的人。
dossiers.registerContextEn: Top banana is informal and mainly associated with North American English. Oxford labels it informal and especially North American, while Collins describes it as slang and mainly American.
dossiers.registerContextZh: top banana 屬非正式用語，主要見於北美英語。 它通常帶有輕鬆、幽默或略帶戲謔的語氣。
dossiers.memoryEn: The top performer became the top banana; today, the top person in a group can still be called the top banana.
dossiers.memoryZh: 最重要的表演者曾被稱為 top banana；今天，一個群體中地位最高的人仍可被稱為 top banana。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use It for a Person
semanticRules.titleZh: 黃女士是部門內的最高話事人
semanticRules.en: Use It for a Person
semanticRules.zh: 黃女士是部門內的最高話事人。 這個國家是最大的香蕉生產國。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Person Must Have the Highest Position or
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則三
semanticRules.en: A popular, experienced or talented person is not automatically the top banana.
semanticRules.zh: 受歡迎、經驗豐富或能力出眾的人，不一定是最高話事人。 語境必須顯示對方擁有最高地位或實際決策權。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Second Banana”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四
semanticRules.en: Second banana means a person in a supporting or less important position. The two expressions developed from the ranking of performers in American show business.
semanticRules.zh: top banana 指首要人物； second banana 則指處於次要或輔助地位的人。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Force “By + V-ing” into Every Answer
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十
semanticRules.en: Do Not Force “By + V-ing” into Every Answer
semanticRules.zh: 規則十

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Leo runs the café and makes every important decision.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: Leo 管理這間咖啡店，並作出所有重要決定。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Leo is the top banana at the café.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: Leo 是咖啡店的最高話事人。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Did Ella take control of the club? B: Yes. The members elected her last Friday.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：Ella 已接管學會嗎？ 乙：是。會員在上星期五選出了她。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Ella became top banana after the members elected her last Friday.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 會員上星期五選出 Ella 後，她成為了學會的最高話事人。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Who should I ask about this large order? B: Speak to Mr Wong. He is our highest-ranking manager.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：這張大額訂單應該詢問誰？ 乙：找黃先生吧。他是我們職位最高的經理。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Ask our top banana, Mr Wong, about the large order.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 關於這張大額訂單，可以詢問我們的最高負責人黃先生。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Peter has an impressive title, so I believed that he controlled the office. In fact, all the staff report to his sister.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: Peter 的職銜看來很重要，所以我以為辦公室由他掌管。其實所有員工都向他的姐姐匯報。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I thought Peter was the top banana, but the staff actually report to his sister.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我以為 Peter 是最高話事人，但員工其實向他的姐姐匯報。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The new owner put Felix in charge of the entire restaurant.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 新店主委任 Felix 掌管整間餐廳。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The new owner made Felix the top banana at the restaurant.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 新店主委任 Felix 成為餐廳的最高負責人。

dossiers.meaningEn: A fashionable group of rich, famous or socially important people whose expensive and glamorous lives receive public attention.
dossiers.meaningZh: 一群時尚、富有、著名或具有社會地位的人；他們過着奢華而引人注目的生活，經常受到公眾及傳媒關注。
dossiers.registerContextEn: The expression is generally neutral to informal.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達一般屬中性至非正式語域。
dossiers.memoryEn: Think of people whose wealth, fashion and public image make their lives appear “beautiful” from the outside.
dossiers.memoryZh: 想像一群人的財富、時尚作風及公眾形象，令他們的生活從外表看來十分「美麗」。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Interpret “Beautiful” Literally
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則一：不要把 beautiful 單純理解為外表漂亮
semanticRules.en: In the target expression, beautiful does not merely describe physical appearance. The five students are very attractive. This sentence contains no information about wealth, fashion, fame or a glamorous social circle.
semanticRules.zh: 在目標表達中，beautiful 並不只是形容外表漂亮。 這五名學生的外表十分漂亮。 這個句子沒有提及財富、時尚、名氣或奢華社交圈，因此不足以使用目標表達。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Assume That Every Rich Person Belongs
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四
semanticRules.en: to the Group; wealth or fame; fashion; glamour; social visibility; an expensive and public lifestyle. A private business owner who avoids attention would not automatically be described as one of the beautiful people.
semanticRules.zh: 不要假設所有富人都是 the beautiful people 這個表達通常不只是表示「有錢」，還帶有時尚、名氣、奢華社交生活及公眾關注等意思。 一名生活低調、不受公眾關注的富有商人，未必適合被形容為時尚名人圈的一員。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Overuse It
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：不要過度使用
semanticRules.en: The expression is useful when the social identity of the group matters.; guests; customers; actors; visitors; rich people; famous people.
semanticRules.zh: 當這群人的時尚、財富、名氣及社會地位與語境有關時，這個表達才特別有用。 如果句子不需要強調這種名流身份，使用普通名詞可能更加準確。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Morally Good People
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：不要用來表示品格善良的人
semanticRules.en: normally refers to a fashionable, wealthy or famous social group.
semanticRules.zh: 兩個句子的意思並不相同。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Rich and fashionable guests often spend their evenings at this famous café.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 富有而時髦的賓客經常在這間著名咖啡店度過晚上。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The beautiful people often spend their evenings at this famous café.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 上流社會的時髦人物經常在這間著名咖啡店度過晚上。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Why do wealthy celebrities and fashion leaders keep choosing this quiet town for their holidays?
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 為甚麼富有的名人及時尚領袖不斷選擇這個寧靜小鎮度假？
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Why do the beautiful people keep choosing this quiet town for their holidays?
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 為甚麼時尚名流不斷選擇這個寧靜小鎮度假？

candidateQuestions.promptEn: While working at the hotel, he used to watch the lives of rich celebrities from behind the front desk.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 他在酒店工作時，經常從接待處後方觀察富有名人的生活。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: He used to watch the beautiful people from behind the hotel’s front desk.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 他以往經常從酒店接待處後方觀察時尚名流。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The article presents wealthy and fashionable social figures as confident and carefree, but its interviews reveal a different picture.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 這篇文章把富有而時髦的社交人物描寫成自信而無憂無慮，但訪問內容卻呈現出不同的景象。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The article presents the beautiful people as confident and carefree, but its interviews reveal a different picture.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 這篇文章把時尚名流描寫成自信而無憂無慮，但訪問內容卻呈現出不同的景象。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: At the private party, several young actors mixed with wealthy and fashionable members of high society.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 在私人派對上，幾名年輕演員與富有而時髦的上流社會人物交際。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: At the private party, several young actors mixed with the beautiful people.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 在私人派對上，幾名年輕演員與時尚名流交際。

dossiers.meaningEn: To receive severe criticism, blame, a strong telling-off or punishment, usually because of something that somebody has done or is believed to have done.
dossiers.meaningZh: 因為自己所做的事情，或被認為要負責的事情，而受到嚴厲批評、責罵、指責或懲罰。
dossiers.registerContextEn: Get it in the neck is informal and particularly associated with British English. It is natural in conversation, informal messages, personal stories, interviews and conversational journalism.
dossiers.registerContextZh: get it in the neck 是非正式表達，尤其常見於英式英語。 它適合用於日常對話、非正式訊息、個人故事、訪問及較口語化的新聞評論。
dossiers.memoryEn: A blow to a vulnerable place represents receiving a particularly severe reaction.
dossiers.memoryZh: 脆弱位置受到重擊的畫面，代表一個人承受十分強烈的負面反應。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use It for Strong Criticism or Punishment
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則三：用於強烈批評或懲罰
semanticRules.en: A polite suggestion is normally not strong enough to license the idiom.
semanticRules.zh: 經理責罵了 Leo 十分鐘。 Leo 被狠狠責罵了一頓。 老師有禮地提出一項小小的改善建議，語氣通常不足以使用這個慣用語。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Add a Second Explanation Unnecessarily
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：不要不必要地再次解釋相同意思
semanticRules.en: The second clause repeats the idiom’s meaning.
semanticRules.zh: 第二個分句重複了慣用語已經表達的意思。 刪除檔案後被經理狠狠責罵。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use the Literal Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：不要使用字面意思
semanticRules.en: The ball hit him in the neck. The exercise teaches only the figurative meaning.
semanticRules.zh: 皮球擊中了他的頸部。 他因弄失皮球而被狠狠責罵。 本練習只教授比喻意思。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Get It”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：不要與 get it 混淆
semanticRules.en: Get it in the neck is the longer fixed target in this lesson.
semanticRules.zh: get it 可以表示「明白」、「接電話或應門」，亦可表示「受罰」。 本課只訓練較長的固定表達 get it in the neck。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Have It in for Someone”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十
semanticRules.en: get it in the neck = receive severe criticism or punishment
semanticRules.zh: 不要與 have it in for someone 混淆受到嚴厲批評或懲罰存心針對某人兩者是不同表達。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use It Naturally, Not Everywhere
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：自然使用，不要過度使用
semanticRules.en: 1. the criticism or punishment is strong; 2. somebody becomes the target; 3. the reason or situation is clear; 4. the tone is informal.
semanticRules.zh: 當批評或懲罰十分強烈、有人明顯成為責罵對象、原因或情境清楚，而且語氣屬非正式時，這個慣用語最為自然。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Liam arrived twenty minutes late, and his teacher severely scolded him.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: Liam 遲到了二十分鐘，因此受到老師嚴厲責罵。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Liam got it in the neck from his teacher after arriving twenty minutes late.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: Liam 遲到二十分鐘後，被老師狠狠責罵了一頓。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The supervisor admitted that he had made the mistake because he did not want the new worker to receive the blame.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 主管承認錯誤是由自己造成，因為他不想讓新員工承受責罵。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Rather than let the new worker get it in the neck, the supervisor admitted his own mistake.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 主管沒有讓新員工受責罵，而是承認了自己的錯誤。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Why are you worried about the meeting? B: I think the boss will strongly criticise me because I missed the target.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：你為甚麼擔心這次會議？ 乙：我覺得老闆會因我未能達到目標而狠狠責罵我。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I think I’ll get it in the neck from the boss for missing the target.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我覺得老闆會因我未能達到目標而狠狠責罵我。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The assistant received a severe telling-off and then corrected the figures immediately.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 助理被狠狠責罵後，立即改正了數字。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: After getting it in the neck, the assistant corrected the figures immediately.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 助理被狠狠責罵後，立即改正了數字。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The club members ignored the clean-up instructions, so the school punished them.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 社團成員無視清潔指示，因此受到學校懲罰。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The club members got it in the neck after ignoring the clean-up instructions.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 社團成員無視清潔指示後受到嚴厲懲罰。

dossiers.meaningEn: a passenger who repeatedly gives a driver unwanted advice; also, a person who tries to control work entrusted to someone else
dossiers.meaningZh: 不斷向司機提供未經要求的意見的乘客；也可比喻沒有直接負責，卻試圖指揮他人工作的人。
dossiers.registerContextEn: interviews; general-interest articles; lightly humorous descriptions.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達屬於非正式用語，適合用於：
dossiers.memoryEn: The person is not holding the wheel, but still tries to direct the journey.
dossiers.memoryZh: 這個人沒有握着軚盤，卻仍然試圖指揮整段旅程。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use “A”, Not “An”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則三：使用 a，而不是 an
semanticRules.en: Back begins with a consonant sound, so use a.
semanticRules.zh: 以輔音開首，因此應使用 a。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Advice Must Normally Be Unwanted
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：意見通常必須是未經要求的
semanticRules.en: The passenger was a back-seat driver. The second passenger is simply providing requested help.
semanticRules.zh: 不適合： 第二個情況中的乘客只是在提供司機主動要求的協助。

semanticRules.titleEn: One Necessary Warning Is Not Enough
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：一次必要警告並不足夠
semanticRules.en: This is one urgent safety warning. This is a continuing pattern of unwanted control.
semanticRules.zh: 通常屬於 a back-seat driver: 以下情況通常不是 a back-seat driver:

semanticRules.titleEn: The Passenger Need Not Literally Sit in the Back
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：乘客不一定真的坐在後座
semanticRules.en: Modern dictionaries define the person generally as a passenger, not only as someone physically sitting in the rear seat. The expression describes the behaviour rather than the exact seat occupied. A person in the front passenger seat can still be a back-seat driver.
semanticRules.zh: 現代字典一般把這個人定義為乘客，而不是只限於真正坐在後座的人。 這個表達重點在於行為， 而不是實際座位。 坐在前排乘客座位的人，仍然可以被稱為 a back-seat driver。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：不要重複相同意思
semanticRules.en: The second clause merely explains the idiom again. Leo is a back-seat driver whenever I drive, and he constantly gives me unwanted driving instructions. Leo is a back-seat driver whenever I drive. The source explains the unwanted instructions. The answer compresses them into the noun phrase.
semanticRules.zh: 較差： 第二個分句只是再次解釋慣用語的意思。 較佳： 原句負責解釋未經要求的指示； 答案以名詞短語把意思濃縮。

semanticRules.titleEn: “Back-Seat Driving” Is Related but Not the Target
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一
semanticRules.en: a back-seat driver back-seat driving
semanticRules.zh: back-seat driving 是相關形式，但並非本課目標相關名詞是： 不過，本練習的所有答案都必須使用：

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Whenever I drive, Leo repeatedly tells me when to slow down, turn and change lanes, although I never ask him for help.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 每當我駕駛時，里奧都會反覆告訴我何時減速、轉彎和轉換行車線，雖然我從沒有請他幫忙。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Leo is a back-seat driver whenever I drive.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 每當我駕駛時，里奧總會在旁不斷指點。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The traffic light has turned red, and I need to warn you. However, I do not want one necessary warning to sound like unwanted driving advice.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 交通燈已轉為紅色，我需要提醒你。不過，我不希望一次必要警告聽起來像未經要求的駕駛指示。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: I do not want to sound like a back-seat driver, but the traffic light has turned red.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我不想聽起來像一個愛在旁指點司機的人，但交通燈已轉為紅色。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: She may sincerely believe that she is helping. Nevertheless, her repeated comments are distracting the driver.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 她可能真心相信自己正在幫忙。不過，她反覆作出的評論令司機分心。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: She may not mean to be a back-seat driver, but she is distracting the driver.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 她可能並非有意在旁不斷指點，但她正在令司機分心。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Nina spoke only once because she saw a child step into the road. It was wrong to describe her as a constantly interfering passenger.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 妮娜只說了一次，因為她看到一名小孩走出馬路。把她形容為不斷干預司機的乘客並不公平。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: It was unfair to call Nina a back-seat driver because she spoke only when she saw real danger.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 說妮娜愛在旁胡亂指點並不公平，因為她只在看到真正危險時才說話。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The former manager no longer runs the company, but he still tries to control the new manager’s decisions from outside.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 前任經理已不再管理公司，但他仍試圖從外部控制新經理的決定。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The former manager has become a back-seat driver in the company he once led.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 前任經理在自己曾經領導的公司中，變成了一個仍然從旁指手畫腳的人。

dossiers.editorialCaution: “Back-seat driver” has a literal passenger and a figurative interference sense; both require unwanted advice or control.

dossiers.meaningEn: A disagreement or conflict that continues for a long time and involves repeated arguments or confrontations on different occasions.
dossiers.meaningZh: 一場持續一段長時間、在不同場合反覆出現的爭執或衝突；持續爭論不休。
dossiers.registerContextEn: The expression is neutral and is common in conversation, journalism, reports and general writing. It usually carries a negative tone because the repeated disagreement has not been settled.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達屬於中性語域，常見於日常對話、新聞報道、報告及一般文章。 由於雙方的爭執一直未能解決，它通常帶有負面語氣。
dossiers.memoryEn: The disagreement keeps moving from one occasion to the next, so it becomes a running battle.
dossiers.memoryZh: 爭執從一個場合延續到下一個場合，因此成為一場持續不斷的 running battle。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use “Between” to Name Both Sides
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：使用 between 同時指出雙方
semanticRules.en: Use “Between” to Name Both Sides
semanticRules.zh: 使用 between 同時指出雙方

semanticRules.titleEn: One Argument Is Not Enough
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：一次爭吵並不足夠
semanticRules.en: The two pupils have argued about the book several times this month.
semanticRules.zh: 這表示爭執已在不同時間反覆出現。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Same Main Conflict Must Continue
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：必須是同一場主要衝突持續出現
semanticRules.en: The separate arguments should normally concern the same central problem. If two people argue once about dinner and later argue about an unrelated film, those events do not necessarily form a running battle.
semanticRules.zh: 不同場合發生的爭執，通常必須圍繞同一個核心問題。 如果兩人先為晚餐爭吵，後來又為一齣毫不相關的電影爭吵，兩件事未必構成同一場 running battle。

semanticRules.titleEn: “Running” Does Not Mean Physical Running Here
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：running 在此不表示奔跑
semanticRules.en: The groups fought while moving through several streets.
semanticRules.zh: 他們一直就泊車問題爭執不下。 各群體一邊移動，一邊在數條街道上打鬥。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Exaggerate a Mild Difference
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十一：不要誇大輕微分歧
semanticRules.en: A running battle requires repeated and noticeable disagreement, not merely different preferences.
semanticRules.zh: 必須涉及反覆而明顯的爭執，而不只是喜好不同。

semanticRules.titleEn: Avoid Unnecessary Violence
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：避免不必要的暴力語境
semanticRules.en: Although battle creates a strong image, the figurative expression does not mean that people are physically fighting.
semanticRules.zh: 雖然 battle 帶有強烈意象，但這個比喻表達並不表示雙方真的動武。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Oliver and his neighbour have argued many times about the noisy gate during the past three months.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 過去三個月，奧利弗與鄰居多次就嘈吵的閘門發生爭執。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Oliver has had a running battle with his neighbour over the noisy gate for three months.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 奧利弗三個月來一直與鄰居就嘈吵的閘門爭執不下。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The school is changing the collection timetable again. This may cause parents to make repeated complaints.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 學校再次更改接放學時間表，這可能會令家長反覆投訴。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: By changing the timetable again, the school may create a running battle with parents over collection times.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 學校再次更改時間表，可能會引起與家長之間有關接放學時間的長期爭拗。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Are you going to complain to the referee after every decision? B: No. I do not want this disagreement to continue for the whole season.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：你是否打算在球證每次作出決定後都投訴？ 乙：不。我不希望這場爭議持續整個球季。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The team captain is trying to avoid a running battle with the referee over every decision.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 隊長正嘗試避免就球證的每項判決與他持續爭論。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The deliveries kept arriving late, so the organiser and several unhappy customers began arguing repeatedly.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 送貨一再延誤，因此主辦者與數名不滿的顧客開始反覆爭論。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The organiser has ended up in a running battle with several unhappy customers over the repeated delays.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 主辦者最終因一再延誤而與數名不滿的顧客持續爭執。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Why must I argue with customer service again and again just to correct one bill? B: I agree. Fixing one bill should be simple.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：為甚麼我只是要更正一張帳單，卻要一次又一次與客戶服務部爭論？ 乙：我同意。更正一張帳單應該很簡單。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: It should not take a running battle with customer service to correct one bill.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 更正一張帳單不應需要與客戶服務部長期爭拗。

dossiers.meaningEn: To continue trying hard to achieve, stop, control or protect something even though success is impossible or very unlikely under the present conditions.
dossiers.meaningZh: 在現有情況下，成功機會極低甚至完全沒有，但仍然努力嘗試達成目標、阻止事情發生、控制問題或保護某事物。
dossiers.registerContextEn: everyday conversation; workplace discussion; news and general-interest writing; reports written in accessible language; personal reflection; descriptions of social or practical problems; stories and interviews.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達屬於中性至較口語的用語。
dossiers.memoryEn: The fighting continues, but the likely result is already against you.
dossiers.memoryZh: 戰鬥仍在繼續，但預期結果已經對你不利。

semanticRules.titleEn: The Situation Must Be Much More Than Difficult
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：情況必須遠比一般困難嚴重
semanticRules.en: The task may be tiring, but the source does not show that failure is very likely.
semanticRules.zh: 一名員工每天要接聽五百個來電，幾乎不可能全部處理。 這項工作可能令人疲倦，但原句沒有顯示失敗機會極高。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “An Uphill Battle”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：不要與 an uphill battle 混淆
semanticRules.en: A difficult struggle that may still succeed. A struggle that is impossible or very unlikely to succeed under the present conditions. Learning all the new software will be an uphill battle, but we have six months and a good teacher.
semanticRules.zh: 一場十分困難但仍有可能成功的抗爭。 在現有情況下，幾乎不可能成功的抗爭。 學會所有新軟件會十分困難，但我們有六個月時間和一名好老師，因此仍可能成功。 在沒有電力和可用電腦的情況下，今天教授這套軟件幾乎不可能成功。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Lose a Battle”
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則七：不要與 lose a battle 混淆
semanticRules.en: The defeat has happened. The struggle is continuing or being considered, but failure is expected. They lost the battle yesterday.
semanticRules.zh: 已經落敗。 抗爭仍在進行或正在考慮中，但預計不會成功。 他們昨天已經在戰役中落敗。 他們仍在努力挽救舊服務，但成功機會極低。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Idiom’s Meaning
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：不要重複慣用語已表達的意思
semanticRules.en: The second clause merely explains the idiom again.
semanticRules.zh: 第二個分句只是在使用慣用語後，再次解釋同一意思。 園丁正與雜草進行一場幾乎無望成功的抗爭。 只剩下十分鐘，團隊要準時完成工作，幾乎已經沒有勝算。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use the Expression Naturally, Not Everywhere
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十二：自然使用，不要過度使用
semanticRules.en: 1. somebody is making a continuing or repeated effort; 2. the problem keeps undoing that effort; 3. the available time, tools, money or help are clearly insufficient; 4. the other force is much stronger; 5. present conditions make success impossible or extremely unlikely.; somebody made one mistake; a task takes a long time; somebody lost one game; a plan is slightly inconvenient; the speaker feels nervous; success requires ordinary effort.
semanticRules.zh: 這個慣用語最自然的使用情況包括： 不要只因以下情況便使用：

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The caretaker mops the entrance again and again, but people keep bringing in rainwater. He is very unlikely to keep the floor dry during the storm.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 看更不斷拖乾入口，但人們一直把雨水帶進來。在暴風雨期間，他幾乎不可能保持地面乾爽。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The caretaker is fighting a losing battle to keep the entrance dry during the storm.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 看更在暴風雨期間不斷嘗試保持入口乾爽，但幾乎注定無法成功。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Before the roof was repaired, the family cleaned the mould repeatedly, but it always returned after rain.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 屋頂維修前，那家人多次清除霉菌，但每逢下雨後霉菌都會再次出現。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Before the roof was repaired, the family had been fighting a losing battle against the mould.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 屋頂維修前，那家人一直徒勞地對付反覆出現的霉菌。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: The manager wants the two of us to answer five hundred emails before lunch. B: That target is almost impossible.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：經理要求我們兩人在午飯前回覆五百封電郵。 乙：這個目標幾乎不可能達到。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: We are fighting a losing battle to answer five hundred emails before lunch.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 我們要在午飯前回覆五百封電郵，幾乎注定無法完成。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: I try to make every customer happy, but they often want opposite things. B: Nobody can satisfy everyone at the same time.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：我嘗試令每位顧客都滿意，但他們往往有互相矛盾的要求。 乙：沒有人可以同時滿足所有人。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Trying to please every customer at once is a losing battle.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 要同時令每位顧客滿意，幾乎是一項不可能成功的任務。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The team keeps correcting false stories online, but ten new stories appear whenever one is removed.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 團隊不斷更正網上的虛假消息，但每刪除一則，便會出現十則新的。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The team seems to be fighting a losing battle against false stories online.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 團隊似乎正與網上不斷出現的虛假消息徒勞抗爭。

dossiers.meaningEn: A pitched battle is a fierce, sustained and strongly contested argument, struggle or competition between opposing sides.
dossiers.meaningZh: a pitched battle 指對立雙方之間非常激烈、持續而且爭持不下的爭論、鬥爭或競爭。
dossiers.registerContextEn: The expression is generally neutral to formal, but strongly dramatic.
dossiers.registerContextZh: 這個表達一般屬中性至正式語域，但語氣相當強烈。
dossiers.memoryEn: Both sides have taken their positions and are fully prepared to fight; neither side is giving way easily.
dossiers.memoryZh: 雙方都已站穩陣地並準備正面交鋒，誰也不願輕易讓步。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Treat “Pitched” as a Reference to Sound
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則三：不要把 pitched 理解為聲音高低
semanticRules.en: a high-pitched voice
semanticRules.zh: 尖銳的聲音一場激烈對抗

semanticRules.titleEn: Use It Only for a Strong Conflict
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四：只用於強烈衝突
semanticRules.en: The two companies fought for months over a major contract, and neither would give way. The two friends disagreed for five minutes about which film to watch. A brief everyday disagreement is normally too weak.
semanticRules.zh: 兩間公司為一份重要合約爭持數月，雙方都不願讓步。 兩名朋友就觀看哪一套電影爭論了五分鐘。 短暫的日常意見分歧通常未達到這個表達所需的強度。

semanticRules.titleEn: Both Sides Must Be Seriously Engaged
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：雙方都必須認真投入對抗
semanticRules.en: A pitched battle normally involves opposing sides that both resist, compete or fight strongly. One group complained, and the other immediately agreed. There is no sustained two-sided struggle.
semanticRules.zh: a pitched battle 通常涉及對立雙方，而雙方都在強烈反抗、競爭或爭取勝利。 一個小組提出投訴，另一個小組立即同意。 這個情境並不存在持續的雙方對抗。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Mix the Literal Military Sense into This Set
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則九：本練習不混入字面軍事意思
semanticRules.en: Oxford records this older military meaning, but this exercise teaches only the modern figurative extension involving intense disputes, struggles and competitions.
semanticRules.zh: 兩軍在平原上列陣交戰。 本練習只教授現代比喻用法，不會把軍事戰役和一般社會爭議混合在同一套題目中。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Overstate an Ordinary Competition
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十：不要誇大普通競爭
semanticRules.en: Both candidates fought hard for months, and the final vote was extremely close. One runner was far ahead and won easily. An easy or one-sided victory is not normally a pitched battle.
semanticRules.zh: 兩名候選人激烈競爭數月，最終票數非常接近。 其中一名跑手遙遙領先，輕易勝出。 輕易或一面倒的勝利通常不適合形容為 a pitched battle。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The two groups argued fiercely and for a long time about the class trip.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 兩個小組就班級旅行展開了長時間的激烈爭論。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The argument over the class trip became a pitched battle between the two groups.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 兩個小組就班級旅行展開的爭論，演變成一場激烈對抗。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: Why are the shop owners preparing for a difficult meeting? B: They expect a fierce struggle with the landlord over the rent.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：為甚麼店主們正在準備一場艱難的會議？ 乙：他們預計會就租金問題與業主激烈爭持。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: The shop owners are preparing for a pitched battle with the landlord over the rent.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 店主們正準備就租金問題與業主展開激烈爭持。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The head teacher expected a short discussion, but parents and staff became involved in a serious and prolonged conflict.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 校長原本預計只會有簡短討論，但家長和員工卻陷入嚴重而持久的衝突。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: What the head teacher expected to be a short discussion turned into a pitched battle between parents and staff.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 校長原本預計只會有簡短討論，結果卻演變成家長和員工之間的激烈衝突。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The residents will fight extremely hard against the building company to keep the playground open.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 居民將與建築公司激烈抗爭，以保留遊樂場。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: To keep the playground open, the residents will fight a pitched battle against the building company.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 居民將與建築公司激烈抗爭，以保留遊樂場。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: A: What may happen if the local centre closes the reading room? B: Local families are ready to oppose the decision very strongly.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 甲：如果本地中心關閉閱覽室，可能會發生甚麼事？ 乙：本地家庭已準備強烈反對這項決定。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: If the local centre closes the reading room, it could face a pitched battle with local families.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 如果本地中心關閉閱覽室，便可能需要與本地家庭展開激烈抗爭。

dossiers.meaningEn: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.
dossiers.meaningZh: 一件涉及兩個人或雙方的事情，通常不能單靠其中一方發生、成功、改善或得到解決。
dossiers.registerContextEn: everyday conversation; friendly advice; workplace discussions; interviews; news commentary; general articles; discussions about relationships, teamwork or agreements.
dossiers.registerContextZh: it takes two to tango 屬於口語至中性的諺語式表達，常見於日常對話、友善勸告、工作討論、訪問、新聞評論及一般文章。
dossiers.memoryEn: A partner dance cannot work through one dancer alone; a two-sided situation cannot work through only one side.
dossiers.memoryZh: 雙人舞不能單靠一名舞者完成；涉及雙方的事情也不能只靠其中一方。

semanticRules.titleEn: Use It Only for a Truly Two-Sided Situation
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則四：只用於真正涉及雙方的情況
semanticRules.en: The situation is not meaningfully two-sided.
semanticRules.zh: 兩位朋友都發出了傷人的訊息，卻互相指責。 一個巴掌拍不響。 如果只有一方作出錯誤行為，而另一方沒有參與，使用這個慣用語便不準確。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Use It to Blame a Victim
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則五：不要用來責怪受害者
semanticRules.en: abuse; harassment; bullying; threats; fraud; an attack; a serious power imbalance; a person who had no meaningful choice or participation. The saying should never be used automatically to suggest that every victim shares responsibility.
semanticRules.zh: 在涉及虐待、騷擾、欺凌、威脅、詐騙、襲擊、嚴重權力不平等，或其中一方根本沒有選擇或參與的情況下，不應使用這個表達來分散責任。 不應自動使用這句話暗示每位受害者都需要承擔責任。

semanticRules.titleEn: Shared Responsibility Does Not Always Mean
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則六：雙方有責任不等於責任必定完全相等
semanticRules.en: It does not scientifically calculate that each side is exactly fifty per cent responsible. The exercise uses clear situations in which both sides have made a meaningful contribution to the problem.
semanticRules.zh: 這個表達通常表示雙方都對情況有所影響，但並不表示雙方的責任在所有情況下都必定完全相等。 本練習只使用雙方都明顯對問題有所影響的情境。

semanticRules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Full Meaning Unnecessarily
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則八：不要不必要地重複完整意思
semanticRules.en: The improved sentence lets the idiom carry the shared-responsibility meaning.
semanticRules.zh: 任何一方都不應只責怪另一方； 一個巴掌拍不響。 改良句讓慣用語本身承擔「雙方都有責任」的意思。

semanticRules.titleEn: “It Takes Two” Is Related but Excluded Here
semanticRules.titleZh: 規則十
semanticRules.en: “It Takes Two” Is Related but Excluded Here
semanticRules.zh: it takes two 是相關縮略形式，但本課不採用

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Leo blamed Sara for their argument, but he also shouted at her and refused to listen.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 里奧把爭吵歸咎於莎拉，但他也向她大叫，而且拒絕聆聽。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: It takes two to tango; Leo should not place all the blame on Sara for their argument.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 一個巴掌拍不響；里奧不應把爭吵的全部責任推給莎拉。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The customer wants one design, while the builder wants another. They must settle the final design together.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 顧客希望採用一個設計，建築商則希望採用另一個設計。他們必須共同決定最終方案。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: It takes two to tango, so the customer and the builder must settle the final design together.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 事情需要雙方配合，因此顧客和建築商必須共同決定最終設計。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: Lily has apologised and offered to meet, but Chloe refuses to answer. Lily cannot repair their friendship alone.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 莉莉已道歉並提出見面，但克洛伊拒絕回覆。莉莉無法獨力修補兩人的友誼。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Lily’s effort alone will not repair her friendship with Chloe; it takes two to tango.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 單靠莉莉的努力無法修補她與克洛伊的友誼；這需要雙方共同努力。

candidateQuestions.promptEn: The adviser explained that the agreement was not moving forward because only one side was willing to change.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 顧問解釋，協議沒有進展，是因為只有其中一方願意作出改變。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: “Because it takes two to tango, the agreement will not move forward while only one side is willing to change,” the adviser explained.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 顧問解釋：「由於協議需要雙方配合，如果只有一方願意改變，事情便不會有進展。」

candidateQuestions.promptEn: One department expects the other department to complete every part of their shared project.
candidateQuestions.promptZh: 一個部門期望另一個部門完成共同項目的所有工作。
candidateQuestions.answerEn: Since it takes two to tango, neither department can expect the other to do all the work.
candidateQuestions.answerZh: 既然事情需要雙方配合，任何一個部門都不能期望另一個部門完成所有工作。

dossiers.editorialCaution: The saying covers contribution to a dispute and mutual participation in an agreement/activity. Do not merge these into one vague key.
